manuscripts.title: Metric-measure limits of subcritical FK and spanning-tree planar maps

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.name: Metric and measure convergence
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1 (Metric and measure convergence).
candidates.statement: For each fixed q ∈ (0, 4) in the FK ensemble, and for the spanning-tree ensemble, there are deterministic positive numbers an → 0 such that (V (Mn), andn, µn) law − − − → n→∞ (S, Dh, µh) in Gromov–Hausdorff–Prokhorov topology on compact metric probability spaces modulo measure- preserving isometry. The limit has the parameter specified above. Convergence holds through all positive integers n; the root and decoration are forgotten.

candidates.label: Theorem 3.2
candidates.name: Contour and surface inputs
candidates.heading: Theorem 3.2 (Contour and surface inputs).
candidates.statement: After fixed deterministic changes of time and height units: (i) The bilateral resolved contour, viewed at time scale m and height scale √ m, converges locally uniformly in law to a two-dimensional Brownian motion with equal coordinate variances and correlation ρ. The empty-word contour at total time 2n, with total rescaled time one, converges to the corresponding quadrant excursion from zero to zero. (ii) The bilateral Brownian contour determines a curve-decorated γ-quantum cone. Its curve η : R → C is continuous, transient, space filling, and parameterized by quantum area. The excursion determines the ordinary unit-area DMS quantum sphere with its area-parameterized space-filling curve. The latter sphere is the quantum-sphere measure disintegrated at area one. (iii) The spatial equivalence relation of the sewing is generated by finite chains of scalar horizontal chords. For a scalar coordinate X, a horizontal chord joins s < t if X(s) = X(t) = inf [s,t] X. At the deterministic or independently sampled cuts used below, the two boundary strands are contour-tree lineages parameterized by quantum boundary length. In the cone coupling, the intrinsic decorated surface of each fixed bounded time interval is determined by its contour increments. This assertion may be used simultaneously for a countable collection of deterministic cuts or cuts sampled independently of the surface, and for later selection among that collection. (iv) On a buffered spatial patch, the imaginary field determines its directed local traversals and their frontier flow lines. Together with the real field and local Poisson area marks, these determine the clocked local pieces, their incoming and outgoing sides, and the quantum lengths of the local frontier arcs. This statement does not determine the global order of separate traversals.

candidates.label: Theorem 3.5
candidates.name: Metric inputs
candidates.heading: Theorem 3.5 (Metric inputs).
candidates.statement: For the fixed subcritical parameter, the LQG metric Dh is a continuous length metric inducing the Euclidean topology. In whole-plane GFF coordinates it is proper and geodesic, and geodesics between each fixed pair of distinct points are almost surely unique. Internal metrics are local in the field. Conformal covariance and Weyl scaling hold: adding a continuous function f multiplies path length locally by eξf . For a compact set K in an ordinary field chart and 0 < χ < ξ(Q − 2), there are almost surely finite random constants controlling connections between nearby points of K inside Euclidean balls of a fixed multiple of their separation by C|z − w|χ. The corresponding internal diameters of small dyadic squares, with a bounded enlargement still in the chart, have the same type of bound. Fixed boxes of bounded aspect ratio admit access to their flat faces by completion of the internal metric. In whole-plane GFF coordinates, strong confluence holds simultaneously for all geodesics: an interior segment of any geodesic persists in all geodesics whose endpoints sufficiently closely approximate slightly longer interior subsegments. The same local assertion holds for short geodesic subarcs in buffered ordinary surface charts. In particular, every nonempty open geodesic subarc contains a segment of a geodesic between points of a deterministic countable dense set.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.2
candidates.name: Exponential bound from square-root tightness
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.2 (Exponential bound from square-root tightness).
candidates.statement: For the iid raw word with fixed bF ∈ (0, 1/2) there are constants c, C > 0 such that, for every integer m ≥ 1 and x ≥ 0, P[Mm > x √ m] ≤ Ce−cx . (4.7) In particular, for some λ > 0 and K < ∞, sup m≥1 E exp{λMm/ √ m} ≤ K. (4.8) The same bounds hold conditionally on any previously observed information under which the raw block remains iid with this law.

candidates.name: Uniformity over exterior typings
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.3 (Uniformity over exterior typings).
candidates.statement: Fix bF ∈ (0, 1/2). Let νbF be the law on C([0, 1], R2) of Brownian motion started from zero with covariance matrix at time t equal to t 2 1 − bF bF bF 1 − bF ! . For the bounded-Lipschitz distance associated with the uniform ℓ1 path metric, sup σ dBL  L(m−1/2 Zσ (m ·)), νbF  −→ 0, (4.9) where σ ranges over all possibly randomized, word-dependent exterior typings. The convergence holds conditionally, uniformly over previously observed data which leave the block fresh and iid. A fixed finite family of deterministic disjoint blocks, whose lengths each tend to infinity, converges jointly to independent Brownian paths after applying the respective square-root normalizations.

candidates.label: Corollary 4.12
candidates.name: Transfer and a finite class bound
candidates.heading: Corollary 4.12 (Transfer and a finite class bound).
candidates.statement: The polarity assertion of Lemma 4.11 holds under every law absolutely continuous with respect to the joint law of the pieces and their starting vectors described above. Under a density bound L ≤ K, its measurable mesh-cover events obey Q(FG,δ ∩ {L ≤ K}) ≤ KCεδβe−m−ε . Mere absolute continuity transfers polarity, without asserting the same polynomial bound for the mesh-cover events under the untruncated law. Suppose a collection of eligible time points has a scalar chord relation in each color, and every fixed finite family of pairwise separated enlarged windows about distinct eligible points has this joint absolute-continuity property. Assume also that every tested finite chord diagram is realized by a continuous completion in a fixed order of those windows, or one of finitely many such orders. Then, almost surely, every class generated by the two chord relations has at most  β β − 1  (4.22) distinct eligible points, provided each finite connected subdiagram of that class uses only eligible points and can be localized in a countable family of such windows.

candidates.label: Proposition 6.4
candidates.name: Degree and robust planar topology
candidates.heading: Proposition 6.4 (Degree and robust planar topology).
candidates.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 6.3, the maps πj have degree +1 or −1 for all sufficiently large j. More precisely, for every ϵ > 0 and sufficiently large j there is a continuous map gj : S2 → Σj with sup z∈S2 dsph(πj(gj(z)), z) < ϵ. Loops with a nonzero projected winding difference robustly separate the corresponding lifted fibers, as specified below; in particular, opposite primal crossings of a rectangle with fixed positive margins intersect in the primal graph.

candidates.label: Corollary 6.6
candidates.name: Primal crossing intersection
candidates.heading: Corollary 6.6 (Primal crossing intersection).
candidates.statement: Assume (T1)–(T3). For sufficiently large j, any two primal graph paths meeting the preceding horizontal and vertical passage tests share a primal vertex. More generally, the assertion holds for any finite configuration of tubes and open ports whose margins permit this test after restricting to subpassages and changing coordinates.

candidates.label: Proposition 6.9
candidates.name: Cellular sewing stability with margins
candidates.heading: Proposition 6.9 (Cellular sewing stability with margins).
candidates.statement: Suppose admissible discrete contour excursions have actual sphere cell complexes, converge uniformly to contours whose finite-chain quotient is a sphere, and satisfy the link approximation and chronological conditions (T1)–(T3) and Equation 6.2. In particular, the scalar approximation hypothesis includes any separately prescribed generators at exceptional or distinguished times. Let z ∈ S2 have finite fiber S = η−1(z), and let J be a finite union of open retained time intervals containing S. Choose closed topological disks about z with E−1 ⋐ int E0 ⋐ int E1 ⋐ int E2 ⋐ int E3 ⋐ int E4, η−1 (E4) ⊂ J. For every fixed integer r ≥ 0 and sufficiently large j, there are nested cellular disks ∆− j ⋐ int ∆+ j such that π−1 j (E0) ⊂ int ∆− j ⊂ ∆− j ⊂ π−1 j (int E1), π−1 j (E2) ⊂ int ∆+ j ⊂ ∆+ j ⊂ π−1 j (int E3). Writing Aj = ∆+ j \ int ∆− j : (i) Aj is a closed cellular annulus and contains π−1 j (E2 \ int E1). (ii) Every original triangle in Sr j (∆+ j ) has its entire chronological interval in J. In particular, taking r ≥ 1 retains complete primal and dual vertex stars of every original triangle meeting the disk. (iii) Every original triangle in Sr j (Aj) has its chronological interval in a fixed compact subset of J \ S, up to an arbitrarily small fixed open time enlargement still contained there. It can therefore be covered by finitely many off-center time blocks, chosen with positive margins. (iv) Robust transverse primal crossings in the annular region have the actual intersections asserted by Corollary 6.6. A closed primal walk there with nonzero projected winding difference about z and a point of S2 \ E4 contains a simple primal circuit surrounding π−1 j (E0). Its chosen interior is contained in ∆+ j , so its interior and the required fixed number of cell-star layers lie in the retained patch. All conclusions are topological. They bound neither the length of an auxiliary joining path nor a normalized endpoint cost.

candidates.label: Corollary 7.2
candidates.name: Noise with a free first displacement
candidates.heading: Corollary 7.2 (Noise with a free first displacement).
candidates.statement: Fix a > 0 and choose HN independently and uniformly from [a √ N, 2a √ N] ∩ Z. Concatenate HN ladder blocks. Writing TN , YN for their duration and second displacement, one has P[(TN , HN , YN ) = (k, m, ℓ)] = 2 aN2 gm/ √ N (k/N, ℓ/ √ N) + o(1)  (7.4) 48 uniformly on compact interior parameter sets of k + m + ℓ ≡ 0 (mod 2). The conditional contour kernel has the continuity and support properties in Lemma 7.1. Conditional on a fixed duration k ∼ tN, the free pair (HN , YN ) has a positive continuous lattice density of order N−1 on m+ℓ ≡ k (mod 2).

candidates.label: Corollary 7.6
candidates.name: Automatic terminal flexible decisions
candidates.heading: Corollary 7.6 (Automatic terminal flexible decisions).
candidates.statement: Fix an enclosing mutable interval strictly inside a positive quadrant excursion and freeze the exterior prefix and suffix. There are positive constants c1, c2 and a terminal collar such that, in a sufficiently small contour tube, all mutable paths stay above mi = ⌊ci √ N⌋, and all provisionally resolved suffix heights in that collar are at most mi. If the mutable interval ends at the fixed suffix entrance heights and the imposed suffix decisions are correct before the collar, every decision in the collar is correct. Consequently the resampled word is empty precisely when its imposed heights stay nonnegative and end at zero.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.9
candidates.name: Macroscopic form of the resampling density
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.9 (Macroscopic form of the resampling density).
candidates.statement: Fix a finite stable decomposition and restrict its macroscopic parameters to a compact set on which all noise durations are positive, all randomized first displacements are strictly inside their support, and the reference height density is positive. Include among the macroscopic nuisance variables the frozen contour pieces, integrated ordinary pieces, and the conditional noise contours. Fix a subsequential limiting law of the actual frozen data. The continuity cells can be chosen so that, for almost every frozen value under this law and every sequence of frozen data converging to that value, the density in Equation (7.7), after multiplication by its common power of N and fixed lattice factor, converges in the form required by Lemma 7.4. Its limit depends only on the macroscopic variables. On every cell containing a compatible strict path tube, its limiting normalizing integral is positive. Here finite frozen data range over atoms having positive probability in the chosen stable cell. In particular, a suffix-type atom comes with an actual compatible word in that cell for the protected-rank comparison.

candidates.label: Theorem 7.10
candidates.name: Common conditional kernels on fixed charts
candidates.heading: Theorem 7.10 (Common conditional kernels on fixed charts).
candidates.statement: Fix a finite collection of protected time charts, fixed instructions, and measurable E-valued observations of their raw words and exact parameters. Extract their independent reference experiments jointly as in Equation (7.5). Consider either the bilateral inventory word or a finite word conditioned to be empty. In the finite case keep every chart in a strict interior time interval. Use the same time and distance units in the reference and actual experiments. In every joint subsequential limit, conditional on the complete limiting contours, the retained cuts and marks locating the charts, and any independently adjoined surface-coordinate data, the observations have the reference kernels evaluated at their chart inputs. For charts in disjoint spatial buffers these kernels are conditionally independent. The assertion includes the universal endpoint observations, not only existential path certificates.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.11
candidates.name: Closure under varying laws and changes of units
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.11 (Closure under varying laws and changes of units).
candidates.statement: Fix the model parameter q. Form the joint array consisting of all marked certificate and universal observations under consideration, their contours and cut data, and the independent reference experiments for a countable list of fixed charts, refinements, instructions and quantum offsets. Use one common Polish array schema, with matching actual and reference readouts in every row. Retain the full canonical joint continuum input: contours, cuts and marks, decorated surface fields, and reference internal metrics on countably many fixed collars. Fix its law in the chosen units; in the bilateral applications this is the scale-covariant continuum law. Its charts have the positive durations, extension lengths, gaps and Brownian-generic inputs required by Theorem 7.10. For finite experiments require also the strict interior endpoint margins of that theorem. Call a law admissible if it is a joint subsequential law of these arrays from the discrete inventory experiments, with this continuum marginal, arbitrary deterministic positive cost units, and every fixed retained time unit tending to infinity in lattice units. The continuum coordinates belong to this same joint approximating coupling and satisfy the conditional-independent augmentation convention at the start of this section; a fixed continuum marginal alone is not the definition of admissibility. The admissible family is closed under further weak extraction, including extraction from a varying sequence of admissible laws. The same holds after deterministic changes of the base quantum units and relabeling the fixed offsets, provided the corresponding discrete arrays are retained and the target continuum marginal has these same genericity and strictness properties. Actual and reference coordinates use identical target time and cost units, and each chart keeps its positive durations, extensions and gaps in its own normalized coordinates. Each reference coordinate has smooth duration and shift densities in its own normalized units; it is not obtained by allowing one old density to degenerate under the changing zoom. Every resulting law has the fixed-chart common-kernel identities of Theorem 7.10; its independent disjoint-chart reference experiments give product conditional kernels. Consequently the spatial, restriction and field-density conclusions below hold anew in that law. Kernels may change with the law: the assertion identifies them with the reference kernels extracted in the new joint array. The fixed full joint continuum marginal remains the same in the further limit.

candidates.label: Theorem 7.13
candidates.name: Local spatial kernels with separate field buffers
candidates.heading: Theorem 7.13 (Local spatial kernels with separate field buffers).
candidates.statement: Let K ⋐ U be a compact confinement in an open real-field domain, and let V be an open imaginary-field domain containing a neighborhood of U. One may alternatively first replace U by any relatively compact neighborhood of K inside it. The limiting local certificate and universal-endpoint observations in K, interpreted with open loss inside U, have conditional kernels measurable in h|U , hIG |V (mod period), area marks in U, O, (7.8) where O is the finite relative global order of the buffered local traversals needed by the observation. Conditional on the complete continuum fields, curve, and marks, observations in disjoint real-field buffers have independent kernels. The imaginary buffers may be larger and may overlap for this conditional-independence assertion. The kernels are intrinsic under changes of the quantum-surface coordinate representation. They are the same in the bilateral and strict-interior finite-excursion experiments with common time and distance units. No fixed positive separation between the test and the real-field boundary is required uniformly across all applications: any prescribed K ⋐ U is allowed before taking the limit.

candidates.label: Corollary 7.14
candidates.name: Field-density transfer and local pasting
candidates.heading: Corollary 7.14 (Field-density transfer and local pasting).
candidates.statement: The spatial kernels in Theorem 7.13 are unchanged under a locally absolutely continuous change of the continuum field law. For a Cameron– Martin modification, work with an actual Gaussian local reference field and a fixed compactly supported smooth real function f in its Cameron–Martin space. In the circle-average-pinned whole-plane reference used below, it suffices to choose the pinning circle outside supp f. One may then use the kernel for h + f on a compact interior patch and retain the kernel for h outside a larger disjoint neighborhood on which f = 0. Conditional on the fields these are the prescribed product kernels. The resulting subprobability comparison is made before selecting a hit or a shortcut event. This is a comparison in the Gaussian reference law; it does not assert that an arbitrary shift preserves the global unit-area normalization of a sphere.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.16
candidates.name: Buffered slot domination
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.16 (Buffered slot domination).
candidates.statement: Consider a finite chronologically ordered list of disjoint slots. In each slot a retained block has a left safety band of positive limiting duration. Conditional on the past before the first slot and on an auxiliary code or marks independent of all fresh letters, the entire list of retained cuts, durations, extension offsets and backwards guard/noise search anchors is fixed before any retained fresh letters are inspected. Independent auxiliary choices have total conditional selection weight at most one. At most one new starting-height difference per 61 coordinate is retained, relative to an earlier observed block. The list of differences is a forest in each coordinate. An arbitrary forest can be put in this form by replacing each component’s tree differences by differences from its chronologically earliest vertex, an integer unimodular change of coordinates. Fix a finite list of flexible-order instructions, and restrict to compact ranges of durations, shifts, ordinary increments and noise parameters on which the guard/noise construction fits in the safety bands and its endpoint density is positive. Consider the subevent on which the specified instructions are genuinely compatible. Under fresh chronological iid sampling, conditional on any incoming past, the joint subprobability law of the raw retained blocks and their exact retained shifts on this subevent is bounded by a fixed constant times an independent raw-block reference law with positive smooth shift densities on its feasible projected lattice. The constant is uniform in N and in the incoming past after the specified compact truncations. It is multiplied only by a finite factor when a finite instruction list is allowed. Arbitrary measurable observations of the blocks obey the same domination.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.18
candidates.name: Null transfer on openly fillable interior charts
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.18 (Null transfer on openly fillable interior charts).
candidates.statement: Consider selected slots as in Proposition 7.16, with no slot meeting a distinguished center time. Suppose their macroscopic input and exact lattice observations have tight absolute continuity relative to the independent reference experiment, obtained for example by Lemma 7.17. Restrict to a protected chart which is openly Brownian fillable: conditional on its retained input there is positive probability of filling the omitted pieces by ordinary Brownian or first-passage bridge pieces so that the chart, with its prescribed signs and gluing instructions, occurs in an ordinary Brownian sewing with strict unused-gap clearance. Any reference-null event for the local observations in that ordinary sewing is also null in the selected limit on this chart. In particular, once an almost-sure open-port crossing estimate has been proved for the ordinary bilateral passage rule in the same units, its failure on such an interior chart has probability zero in the selected limit. No absolute continuity at the omitted distinguished center is asserted.

candidates.label: Corollary 8.6
candidates.name: Comparison from annuli
candidates.heading: Corollary 8.6 (Comparison from annuli).
candidates.statement: Assume the hypotheses of Lemma 8.5 hold simultaneously at every point of every compact subset, along arbitrarily fine families. If the charged quantity is D-length and the boundary connections are passage connections, then the port upper comparison is A/a. If the charged quantity is certificate cost and the boundary connections are D-connections, then every certificate compactly in U costs at least (a/A)DU (x, y).

candidates.label: Proposition 8.14
candidates.name: Amplification
candidates.heading: Proposition 8.14 (Amplification).
candidates.statement: Suppose the family has the annulus transfer property, the certificate operations and continuum joining above, and finite optimal comparisons 0 ≤ c < C < ∞. Suppose the comparisons with the same numerical constants hold at every indexed quantum scale and pass to further extractions. Then: (i) There are fixed shell collars and b > 0 such that, for each δ > 0 and all sufficiently large N, more than three quarters of the labels i ∈ [N, 2N] have probability at least b of a geodesic traversal P with FW (P(0), P(1)) ≥ (C − δ) lenD(P). Here P crosses a fixed closed band, minimizes in its fixed open collar W, and its entire range is contained in that closed band. Its endpoints have fixed positive Euclidean separation. The collars and b do not depend on δ. (ii) For each c1 ∈ (c, C) there are b1 > 0, ρ > 0 and fixed rectangular collars such that more than three quarters of the labels in every sufficiently late window have probability at least b1 of a rectangular certificate of cost a < c1DR+ (x, y). Its endpoints lie on opposite faces of a rectangle R of crossed width at least ρ and aspect ratio between 1/2 and 2, and its entire range is contained in the closed rectangle R. This closed envelope is part of the retained witness. Its slightly larger open collar is used for certificate realizations, and R+ is a further open rectangular denominator collar. One may impose deterministic positive lower and finite upper bounds on the denominator, together with compact internal metric moduli in a further collar.

candidates.label: Proposition 8.15
candidates.name: Equality tangent
candidates.heading: Proposition 8.15 (Equality tangent).
candidates.statement: In addition to Proposition 8.14, suppose the common-kernel family is closed under joint extraction of its fixed quantum offsets and its full marked certificate records, as in Definition 8.2(iv). Suppose its reference internal metrics on fixed collars retain their actual joint law in these extractions. Then a further law has, separately with positive probability, a saturated nonconstant geodesic segment at upper factor C and a rectangular shortcut of ratio at most C −δ0, where δ0 > 0 is deterministic. The shortcut retains its closed rectangular envelope and its endpoints on opposite envelope faces, as in Proposition 8.14(ii). Under local field equivalence and strong confluence, the saturation event can be written for deterministic anchors a0 ̸= a1, rational 0 < t1 < t2 < 1, and a fixed bounded open U as P([t1, t2]) ⋐ U, FU (P(t1), P(t2)) = C(t2 − t1)D(a0, a1), (8.15) where P is the unique fixed-anchor geodesic, parametrized by fractional length. Only the public strong-confluence assertion that a nonempty geodesic subarc contains a segment of a geodesic between points of a deterministic countable dense set is used.

candidates.label: Proposition 8.26
candidates.name: Conditional availability of a finite catalogue
candidates.heading: Proposition 8.26 (Conditional availability of a finite catalogue).
candidates.statement: Consider favorable normalization indices v and a family of passage kernels. Suppose: (i) For each open preservation patch V , the restricted certificate kernel is a function of h|V , the local imaginary traversal data, and their finite genuine order. The order depends only on the imaginary field, and the kernels are compatible under restriction to smaller open patches. Separated restrictions have conditional product kernels. (ii) Under a common normalized background-field law, at every favorable index there is probability at least β > 0 of a strict low-ratio certificate whose entire range lies in a retained closed rectangular envelope and whose endpoints lie on its opposite faces, with common geometric slack and a denominator in a fixed buffered domain. The fixed reference-metric moduli and finite-domain connection bounds are almost surely finite. (iii) The exact affine and volume-normalization identities of the joint kernel family transport each trial to the corresponding favorable reference index after its real coarse constant, spatial logarithm, and fixed volume displacement have been compensated. These are identities of transported fields and deterministically normalized observations, not a Weyl rule for a fixed passage object. (iv) The normalized GFF harmonic profiles, after removing the real coarse constant and reducing the imaginary constant modulo its period, have uniformly tight interior smooth norms on fixed-ratio buffered trial disks. For every θ > 0, one can choose finitely many disjoint buffered trials, a finite deterministic grid of exact real shifts, and the metric bounds for a finite forcing catalogue so that, uniformly over favorable indices, the completed catalogue is available with probability at least 1 − θ. The good event can include fixed bounds on all the resulting Cameron–Martin pairings. No continuity of passage costs under rounding a field shift is required.

candidates.label: Proposition 8.28
candidates.name: Rigidity from local forcing
candidates.heading: Proposition 8.28 (Rigidity from local forcing).
candidates.statement: Suppose the comparison family satisfies the hypotheses of Proposition 8.15. Assume in addition that the positive-probability rectangular shortcuts can be amplified to a high-probability shell event with a finite deterministic catalogue satisfying Lemma 8.19. The event must include the following data, with constants independent of the scale: (a) regular upper and lower reference bounds of order w = (Mλ−i)p, and a shortcut with denominator in [a′λ−ip, A′λ−ip]; (b) shifts of uniformly bounded amplitude and Dirichlet energy, constant on the complete real-field dependency patch of the retained shortcut, vanishing on the preserved exterior patch; (c) the likelihood clipping of Lemma 8.16, imposed before applying Lemma 8.12; 91 (d) output-observable shell traversal events with a lower reference cost κw and the bounded overlap and alignment multiplicities in Remark 8.18. Assume the exact local product kernels permit the completion and preservation in Lemma 8.16. Then the optimal comparisons coincide, c = C, and FU = CDU for every open U.

candidates.label: Theorem 8.30
candidates.name: Identification of local passage laws
candidates.heading: Theorem 8.30 (Identification of local passage laws).
candidates.statement: Fix γ ∈ [ √ 2, 2) and λ > 1. Let a family of local passage laws satisfy Definition 8.2 and the reference metric inputs stated above. Suppose a law in this family has a finite positive deterministic optimal upper comparison 0 < C < ∞, with its comparison bounds retained at its fixed quantum offsets and further extractions. Then its optimal lower comparison equals C, and FU (x, y) = CDh(x, y; U) on every ordinary open chart U, with compact confinement and exhaustion as above. The multiplier C is deterministic for the entire joint law. This theorem gives no estimate for a prescribed discrete endpoint.

candidates.label: Proposition 8.31
candidates.name: Two-sided shell tests control relative units
candidates.heading: Proposition 8.31 (Two-sided shell tests control relative units).
candidates.statement: Work in the physical passage and annulus-transfer framework of Definition 8.2 and Lemma 8.12, with the comparisons of Corollary 8.6 available. Let Gi, i ≥ i0, be own-unit rules with positive deterministic normalization coefficients bi. Assume that, for every base i, its actual relative-offset laws under the intrinsic transport and quantum-unit identities (8.2)–(8.4) are (bi+ℓ/bi)Gi+ℓ in the base i reference units. In particular these are the conditional kernels on the physical annuli to which the annulus-transfer estimates apply. Suppose every Gi satisfies, with probability above the annulus transfer threshold, fixed shell tests with constants 0 < m < M < ∞: lower crossing bounds m for the passage rule and reference metric, surrounding upper bounds M for both, and an upper crossing bound M for each with endpoints to which the other’s lower bound applies. Then there is T < ∞, depending only on m, M and the fixed geometry, such that T−2 ≤ bi/bj ≤ T2 for all i, j ≥ i0.

candidates.label: Proposition 9.5
candidates.name: Lower-barrier initialization
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.5 (Lower-barrier initialization).
candidates.statement: Assume the following assertions for arbitrary deterministic cost normalizations and the same fixed buffered tests. (a) Every sequence of finite-cost crossing witnesses has a subsequential certificate retaining a fixed positive spatial advance. The common-kernel and annulus transfer properties hold in these limits. (b) At unscaled cost, the largest projected advance of every path using at most k edges tends to zero in probability, for each fixed k, uniformly in the compact testing region. (c) A winding circuit used in Xj contains a subpath tested by a fixed finite collection of these crossing tests. The probability and cost thresholds have strict margins, so failure of their high-probability lower test retains a finite-cost witness with probability bounded away from zero. Then, for the finite circuit quantiles in Equation (9.1), lim sup j→∞ j−1 log4 Aj ≥ p.

candidates.label: Proposition 9.8
candidates.name: Comparison at exact-power records
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.8 (Comparison at exact-power records).
candidates.statement: Assume the certificate, spatial-kernel, coordinate-transport, and extraction properties used above. Choose the quantile level α sufficiently close to one for Lemma 8.12, including reference crossing lower bounds in its local event. Suppose a joint extraction in units Aj has lim sup j Aj−i/Aj ≤ K4−ip , i ≥ 0, where K < ∞ is deterministic. Then its port rule has a finite positive deterministic optimal upper comparison C. The same numerical upper bound is valid at every fixed quantum index and on the full cone atlas before changing its own cost normalization. If the family satisfies Definition 8.2, then this rule satisfies FU = CDU .

candidates.label: Proposition 9.11
candidates.name: First-failure propagation
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.11 (First-failure propagation).
candidates.statement: Assume the preceding framework and common- kernel hypotheses, including closure under varying-law extraction with all fixed-offset reference experiments retained as in Proposition 7.11. Assume that the robust lower tests of Proposition 9.5 and the finite catalogue of Proposition 8.28 have been verified for the FK certificate family. Assume also that the strict winding transfer rules of Lemma 9.9 hold at all fixed offsets. Then there are deterministic J, m, R, K and s = p/2 > 0 such that all sufficiently large scales satisfy adjacent ratio bounds in [R−1, R], Aj−m/Aj ≤ 4−sm, and the high-probability lower shell tests. Consequently Equation (9.4) holds.

candidates.label: Proposition 9.12
candidates.name: Verification for the FK certificate family
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.12 (Verification for the FK certificate family).
candidates.statement: The bilateral FK certificate fam- ily constructed in the preceding framework and localization sections satisfies the hypotheses of Proposition 9.11.

candidates.label: Corollary 9.13
candidates.name: Bilateral comparison
candidates.heading: Corollary 9.13 (Bilateral comparison).
candidates.statement: For the fixed FK parameter, every sequence of bilateral time units tending to infinity has a further joint extraction, normalized by B(n), with FU = CDh(·, ·; U) simultaneously in all strict intrinsic charts. The multiplier C is deterministic for that extraction and belongs to a fixed compact subset of (0, ∞). Upper comparisons follow paths inside any open clearance; lower comparisons apply to all compactly confined certificates and use the intrinsic metric of their confinement. Also B(n) → ∞ and Equation (9.4) holds. This conclusion concerns crossing data and infimal continuum costs, and supplies no uniform estimate for arbitrary discrete endpoints.

candidates.label: Corollary 10.2
candidates.name: Discarding large comparison errors
candidates.heading: Corollary 10.2 (Discarding large comparison errors).
candidates.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 10.1, for every η > 0 the number of consecutive comparisons with Ei > η, summed over all components, is at most 6 η m X v=1 ωv. All remaining comparisons have both representative height error and wall error at most η.

candidates.label: Proposition 10.15
candidates.name: Fixed-code arm test
candidates.heading: Proposition 10.15 (Fixed-code arm test).
candidates.statement: Let λ = log R. In the finite shifted address model, fix a code, let mj be its number of occupied boxes at level j, and let ej be the sum of its two monochrome ranks. Put T = X j mj, E = X j ej, 118 and let M be the number of terminal entries. For each ζ > 0, one can choose a fixed sufficiently large R and sufficiently small fixed deletion tolerances so that, as the minimum sampling radius tends to infinity, P{the code’s chord constraints are realizable} ≤ exp{−βλE + ζλT + CR,ζM}. (10.23) The statement is for codes with the regular-slot deletion bound of Lemma 10.8. It is uniform over such finite codes and over arbitrary exact chord endpoints inside their recorded boxes. Small fixed errors in sampling radii or inward integer rounding are absorbed by increasing the minimum permitted radius.

candidates.label: Proposition 10.16
candidates.name: Exponential occupancy bound
candidates.heading: Proposition 10.16 (Exponential occupancy bound).
candidates.statement: Put β = 1/2+d2 > 1. Assume the fixed-code test of Proposition 10.15 in the following quantitative form: for every sufficiently small ζ > 0, choose a fixed boundary tolerance sufficiently small and a fixed R sufficiently large so that, once the minimum radius is sufficiently large, every favorable admissible decorated code c satisfies P{c is realized} ≤ exp   −βλE(c) + ζλT(c) + CR,ζM(c) . (10.24) This estimate is required uniformly in the fixed displacement U. The realization event includes all the actual marked chord constraints. The fractional boundary deletions are absorbed into the ζλT term, and the structural deletions into the explicit terminal term, using the bounded number of sorted-chain charges at each deleted vertex. The fixed-code estimate includes its oscillation exceptions. No such estimate is asserted here for codes whose slots are predominantly irregular. Then there are C, c, C1 > 0, independent of any fixed finite exploration cutoff, such that for all sufficiently large N and all u ≥ 0, P{A ≥ CN + u} ≤ C1 exp(−cN − cu). (10.25) The estimate holds for any word-dependent selection of witness lists made before U. It also holds for a fixed reference grid, and with A replaced by its maximum over grid displacements. The threshold in “sufficiently large” may depend on the fixed exploration cutoff. If Equation (10.8) holds, then EQN A = O(N). (10.26) The corresponding code has length at most a deterministic constant times N with QN -probability tending to one. At an independently and uniformly sampled level j ∈ {0, . . . , J}, EQN mj = O(1).

candidates.label: Proposition 10.18
candidates.name: Rank credit
candidates.heading: Proposition 10.18 (Rank credit).
candidates.statement: Let ε = β − 1 > 0. Consider the projected witness systems of the address construction on logarithmic levels [0, bN], with h bases in an interval of length O(ne−N ). Suppose their pairwise time distances exceed the largest address-cell width used on [aN, bN], where 1 < a < b; thus they occupy distinct boxes there for every displacement. All selected laws satisfy QN ≤ eo(N)P. Then the following combination of events has probability tending to zero: outside a vanishing fraction of levels in [aN, bN], every connected component containing a base has a rank cycle. Here a − 1 is chosen sufficiently small relative to ε(b − a), and then h sufficiently large, with all choices fixed before the scaling limit. Witness-list cutoffs may increase only along the sparse diagonals allowed by the address construction.

candidates.label: Corollary 10.20
candidates.name: Central oscillations at intermediate levels
candidates.heading: Corollary 10.20 (Central oscillations at intermediate levels).
candidates.statement: For a projected address code, assign to every occupied node v an interval of length at most Arv centered within its location cell, where A is fixed and rv is its viewing radius. Centers rounded using the terminal address are also allowed, provided they lie in the specified cell. Write Sv = oscIv Z √ rv . Suppose EQ P j mj = O(N), the expected code length is O(N), and the selected density bound is eO(N). Then EQ X v Sv = O(N). In particular, the sum of the central oscillation amplitudes of the occupied lines has bounded first moment at a uniform intermediate viewing level. The constants may depend on the fixed grid ratios, padding, and A, but not on the exploration-list cutoff.

candidates.label: Proposition 11.5
candidates.name: Saturated centers and actual colored witnesses
candidates.heading: Proposition 11.5 (Saturated centers and actual colored witnesses).
candidates.statement: Assume Equation (11.4). There is a subsequence and deterministic Hj, kj, Lj → ∞ such that Lj = o(Tj) and Lj = o(log Hj) with the following properties. Choose a finite set of centers Cj at the seed level Yj, then independently choose Uj ∼ Unif[0, Lj] and put Xj = Yj − Uj. The centers have a finite limiting count K with EK ≤ C, remain mutually divergent in rj(Xj) units, and have tight access depths. At both Vj = Yj and Vj = Xj, for every fixed k, lim A→∞ lim sup j→∞ Qj " sup t∈Rj,k(Vj) dist(t, Cj) rj(Vj) > A # = 0. (11.5) Finite access witnesses and finitely many actual colored edges can be chosen simultaneously so that their access depths are tight and all their within-line time offsets collapse after coarsening. The limiting colored graph contains every edge which is witnessed by an actual link at bounded reach and bounded line coordinates at the coarsened level.

candidates.label: Corollary 11.11
candidates.name: Tightness of retained height differences
candidates.heading: Corollary 11.11 (Tightness of retained height differences).
candidates.statement: In the preceding stationary extraction, fix a coordinate and group centers whose normalized height differences have finite limits. Within each such group those limits are zero. Every finite forest of relative start heights between retained off-origin blocks in the group is tight, and its joint continuum law with the block increments has the reference absolute continuity of Lemma 11.10.

candidates.label: Corollary 11.13
candidates.name: Interline partners belong to one scalar class
candidates.heading: Corollary 11.13 (Interline partners belong to one scalar class).
candidates.statement: An actual scalar link whose endpoints have bounded coordinates on two distinct enrolled lines has endpoints on lines in the same scalar center class in every subsequential limit.

candidates.label: Theorem 11.19
candidates.name: Finite acyclic contour sewing
candidates.heading: Theorem 11.19 (Finite acyclic contour sewing).
candidates.statement: Let L, R : [0, T] → [0, ∞) be continuous, zero at the endpoints and strictly positive in between. On the circle C = [0, T]/(0 = T), let ∼c be the scalar contour relation s ∼c t ⇐⇒ c(s) = c(t) = min u∈[s,t] c(u), c ∈ {L, R}, with ordered representatives and the endpoint convention. Let ∼ be the relation generated by the two scalar relations. Suppose: (i) a finite constant M bounds the cardinality of every ∼-class; (ii) for every ∼-class E, the bipartite multigraph with vertices the L-classes and the R-classes in E, and one edge for each t ∈ E joining its two scalar classes, is a tree. Then C/ ∼ is homeomorphic to the sphere. The quotient map is continuous and its fibers are exactly the ∼-classes.

candidates.label: Corollary 11.21
candidates.name: One distinguished class
candidates.heading: Corollary 11.21 (One distinguished class).
candidates.statement: In Theorem 11.19, suppose a finite distinguished set S is exactly one combined class, its incidence graph is a tree, and no scalar relation joins S to its complement. Suppose on the complement of S and the common endpoint there is joint Brownian absolute continuity on every finite family of separated compact time intervals, including their relative starting heights. Then the completed quotient is a sphere.

candidates.label: Proposition 11.28
candidates.name: Circuits from protected annuli
candidates.heading: Proposition 11.28 (Circuits from protected annuli).
candidates.statement: Suppose an acyclic center component at a uniform level Xj ∈ [aNj, bNj] admits the following construction, with probability tending to one on that event. It has a retained auxiliary disk and a compact annulus around the component point such that: 152 (i) the original lattice patch agrees with the auxiliary patch by Lemma 11.23, including the full stars needed for separation; (ii) the preimage of the inner disk contains a time neighborhood of each relevant base of radius δjrj(Xj), where δ−1 j is tight; the full preimage of the closed outer disk lies in finitely many retained intervals, each of length at most Mjrj(Xj), with both the number and Mj tight; (iii) finitely many tube crossings of the annulus, arranged to intersect successively and to wind around the inner disk, have total all-edge cost CjB(rj(Xj)), with Cj tight; (iv) all these patches lie in the required base spatial neighborhood. Assume 1 < a0 < a < b, s′ < s, and B(r)/B(nj) ≤ K(r/nj)s on the used lattice scales. Then the original map has a surrounding circuit of cost at most B(nj)e−s′Nj with probability tending to one. Its interior contains the base time neighborhood of radius nje−bNj and its closed interior contains no uninterrupted contour time interval of length nje−a0Nj .

candidates.label: Proposition 11.30
candidates.name: Acyclic components admit cheap circuits
candidates.heading: Proposition 11.30 (Acyclic components admit cheap circuits).
candidates.statement: Use the simultaneous all-seed construction of Lemma 11.6, the address-occupation estimate, Corollary 10.20, and Remark 10.21. Also use Propositions 7.16 and 7.18, the bilateral interior crossing comparison of Corollary 9.13, and Proposition 6.9. Fix 1 < a0 < a < b and 0 < s′ < s. For a uniform view level in [aNj, bNj], the probability that a base belongs to an acyclic combined center component but has no genuine surrounding circuit with the cost and time bounds of Proposition 11.28 tends to zero. The circuit may be confined to any base spatial neighborhood on which the finite-chain typicality cutoff holds.

candidates.label: Proposition 12.3
candidates.name: Circuit sparsity input
candidates.heading: Proposition 12.3 (Circuit sparsity input).
candidates.statement: Use the constants above and the available-circuit definition with the scales in Equation (12.5). Let En,N be the event that some chronological interval of length at most T, in the tested compact window, contains h pairwise ℓ-separated bad times. Along every sequence for which N −→ ∞, ne−bN −→ ∞, there is no sequence of probability laws Qn,N supported on En,N and the preselected master events just described, with e−N ≤ ρn → 0, such that Qn,N ≤ exp(κn,N )Pn, κn,N = o(N). (12.6) The same assertion holds for any fixed constant multiple of T and for sufficiently small fixed spatial neighborhoods inside the selected confinement.

candidates.label: Proposition 12.6
candidates.name: Chronological endpoint modulus
candidates.heading: Proposition 12.6 (Chronological endpoint modulus).
candidates.statement: Assume Equation (12.3) and Proposi- tion 12.3. In a bilateral contour coupling, let J be a compact time interval whose limiting curve image has a neighborhood compactly contained in an open set U. Then, for every deterministic δn ↓ 0, 1 B(n) sup i,j∈nJ∩Z |i−j|≤nδn dGn,U vn(i), vn(j)  −→ 0 in probability. The assertion also holds locally on the event that the stated compact-containment condition is satisfied, by exhausting its clearance and the chronological and spatial compactness cutoffs.

candidates.label: Proposition 12.7
candidates.name: Local endpoint joining
candidates.heading: Proposition 12.7 (Local endpoint joining).
candidates.statement: Assume Proposition 12.6, Lemma 6.1, and the compact sewing interface (T1)–(T3) of Section 6, with vanishing projected edge diameters. In a joint extraction on such a chart, arbitrary primal-vertex endpoints whose continuum locations approach the same point can be joined at cost o(B(n)), with the path confined to any prescribed open neighborhood of that point. The conclusion is uniform over endpoints in a fixed compact chart, in the usual sequential sense. The same conclusion applies in a bilateral exhaustion whenever the tested vertices have tight chronological representatives in its compact sewings.

candidates.label: Corollary 12.8
candidates.name: Bilateral endpoint modulus
candidates.heading: Corollary 12.8 (Bilateral endpoint modulus).
candidates.statement: Under their respective hypotheses, the chronological and spatial endpoint conclusions of Propositions 12.6 and 12.7 hold simultaneously.

candidates.label: Theorem 13.1
candidates.name: Mullin encoding and its infinite version
candidates.heading: Theorem 13.1 (Mullin encoding and its infinite version).
candidates.statement: Rooted spherical map–spanning-tree pairs with n edges are in bijection with length-2n axial walks starting at the origin, remaining in Z2 ≥0, and ending at the origin. The reconstruction is (13.2)– (13.3), with the contour order supplying the embedding and root. Thus uniform pairs correspond exactly to the walk conditioned on this excursion event. Applying the bilateral sewing gives the uniform infinite spanning-tree decorated planar map M.

candidates.label: Theorem 13.2
candidates.name: Peanosphere and interval surfaces
candidates.heading: Theorem 13.2 (Peanosphere and interval surfaces).
candidates.statement: The following statements hold at γ = √ 2. 1. A γ-quantum cone decorated by an independent space-filling SLE8 curve η, subsequently parameterized by µh-area with η(0) = 0, has a bilateral boundary-length process Z = (L, R) with independent Brownian coordinates. The process determines the decorated quantum surface up to its conformal coordinate equivalence. 2. For the ordinary unit-area sphere, the corresponding area-parameterized curve has duration one, with η(0) = η(1), and its boundary-length process consists of two independent Brownian excursions. It determines the decorated sphere. 3. On the cone, for a deterministic finite interval [a, b], the restricted increments (Zt − Za)a≤t≤b determine the abstract quantum surface η([a, b]), its restricted curve, and its incoming and outgoing boundary arcs with their quantum lengths. The determination is modulo conformal maps. Abstract decorated surfaces from disjoint bilateral intervals are independent. For the sphere, the same reconstruction holds on [δ, 1 − δ] for every fixed 0 < δ < 1/2, with its excursion increment law.

candidates.label: Theorem 13.3
candidates.name: Reference metric
candidates.heading: Theorem 13.3 (Reference metric).
candidates.statement: With one deterministic normalization fixed, the γ-LQG metric Dh is a measurable function of h, is a length metric, and induces the conformal-chart topology. Its internal metric Dh(·, ·; U) is determined by h|U . For continuous f, Dh+f (x, y) = inf P:x→y Z len(P;Dh) 0 eξf(P(t)) dt, (13.8) where the infimum is over Dh-rectifiable paths parameterized by Dh-length. For conformal ϕ : U → V , Dh◦ϕ+Q log |ϕ′|(x, y; U) = Dh(ϕ(x), ϕ(y); V ). (13.9) On the whole plane geodesics exist between all points, and for each fixed pair the geodesic is almost surely unique. The metric extends intrinsically to the cone and sphere; the unit-area sphere is almost surely a nondegenerate compact metric space.

candidates.label: Proposition 13.4
candidates.name: Background locality
candidates.heading: Proposition 13.4 (Background locality).
candidates.statement: The following properties concern the fields, curve, and marks. 1. On disjoint buffered subdomains of a GFF chart, conditioning on the exterior gives independent zero-boundary GFF parts and exterior-measurable harmonic parts, for each of the two fields. For changes of the real reference field, fix one pinning circle outside all the subdomains and 166 their dependency buffers; the imaginary constant is interpreted modulo its angular period. On compact patches inside the cone’s unit disk and away from zero, the actual normalized real-field law is locally equivalent to this GFF restriction. The sphere has the corresponding local absolute continuity modulo constants for background properties invariant under constant shifts. Its metric law will instead be transferred using the excursion encoding in Section 19. 2. For an open U and a positive spatial buffer contained in a chart, b h on that buffer determines all oriented curve segments between entrance into and exit from U. The real field gives their quantum-area parametrization and the quantum lengths of their directed frontier arcs. 3. Add a Poisson point process of area times of intensity ε−1, independent of the surface and curve. The cells between consecutive marks which are compactly contained in U, with their directions and frontier lengths, are determined by the two local fields and the spatial marks in U. Conditional on the two fields, the spatial marks form a Poisson process of intensity ε−1µh and have independent restrictions to disjoint open sets. Nested Poisson refinements may be used with their level labels.

candidates.label: Proposition 13.5
candidates.name: Dense-pair coverage of geodesic subarcs
candidates.heading: Proposition 13.5 (Dense-pair coverage of geodesic subarcs).
candidates.statement: Let h be a whole-plane GFF and fix a countable dense set Q ⊂ C. Almost surely, every nonempty open subarc of every nonconstant Dh-geodesic contains a nonconstant subsegment of the geodesic between some two points of Q. The same local conclusion holds for geodesic subarcs in buffered field charts on the cone or sphere, with internal metrics used for the localization.

candidates.label: Proposition 15.1
candidates.name: Certificate limit
candidates.heading: Proposition 15.1 (Certificate limit).
candidates.statement: Suppose a sequence of bilateral sewing models satisfies the interval modulus and moment bounds of Lemmas 14.2 and 14.3, with Bn → ∞. There is a joint subsequential certificate limit with the following properties, almost surely. 1. Every finite-cost certificate has approximating paths along the selected subsequence. Con- versely, every sequence of paths with bounded costs and with ranges in a fixed compact subset of an open coordinate chart has a certificate subsequence. The same assertions hold with any fixed finite number of ordered subpaths marked. 2. If K ⋐ U, endpoints converging to the same point of K can be joined at costs tending uniformly to zero by paths in U. This holds for discrete endpoints, limiting endpoints, and mixtures of the two in the contour coupling. 3. Certificates concatenate finitely, with the sum of their costs and with arbitrarily small additional cost in an arbitrary open enlargement of their ranges. They can be cut by marking approximating paths and extracting further. 4. Let FU (x, y) be the infimum of the costs of certificates from x to y with compact range in U. On each connected open U this is a finite continuous pseudometric. For V ⊂ U one has FU ≤ FV wherever both are defined. All these assertions are compatible with further certificate extractions. The assertion about continuity is local in U × U; it does not assert convergence of distances constrained to the boundary of a fixed closed set.

candidates.label: Proposition 15.5
candidates.name: Spatial product kernels
candidates.heading: Proposition 15.5 (Spatial product kernels).
candidates.statement: For every open coordinate domain U, the collection of all certificates with compact range in U has a regular conditional law KU (h|U , b h|U ; ·) depending only on the restrictions of the two fields to U. If U1, . . . , Um are disjoint open sets, these collections are conditionally independent given the complete fields, with respective conditional laws KUi . These laws are consistent under restriction and exhaustion. They also exist on the free-field patches obtained by local absolute continuity in Proposition 13.4. Here the local collection retains projected endpoints and ranges, costs, and ordered-subpath incidences; the original global contour-time labels have been forgotten. Relative parametrizations inside locally retained cells may be used during the construction. In particular one can preserve a sampled collection on each of finitely many disjoint patches and complete it to a sample of the whole certificate law, provided that the preserved collections have the specified product conditional law for the new fields on those patches. This statement concerns conditional sampling; it makes no assertion that the competitor satisfies a Weyl rule.

candidates.label: Proposition 15.9
candidates.name: Intrinsic transport and fixed quantum units
candidates.heading: Proposition 15.9 (Intrinsic transport and fixed quantum units).
candidates.statement: The local kernels of Proposi- tion 15.5 can be chosen consistently under restriction so that the following law identities hold. 1. For every fixed conformal coordinate map ϕ : U → V , the pullback of the conditional certificate law on V is the conditional law on U at the pulled-back fields e h = h ◦ ϕ + Q log |ϕ′ |, e b h = b h ◦ ϕ − χ arg ϕ′ . This is intrinsic coordinate covariance in law. 2. For fixed v > 0, put cv = γ−1 log v and define the new normalized law K (v) U (g, b g; ·) := (Sv−p )#KU (g + cv, b g; ·). (15.12) As a transformation of the joint law, this gives the real field its translated marginal, namely the law of h − cv, and preserves the restriction and product-kernel properties on every U. On the buffered reference patches of Proposition 13.4, local equivalence also defines it under the unchanged Gaussian reference marginal. It need not equal KU . For the established metric one has v−p Dg+cv = Dg. (15.13) 3. All fixed dyadic v can be retained in one joint extraction. In the time-2j, cost-Aj experiment, the law in Equation (15.12) uses time resolution 2j−i and cost denominator Aj2−ip when v = 2−i. Consequently, if the level j − i is also expressed in its own Aj−i units, its deterministic conversion factor is bi = 2ip lim j Aj−i Aj , (15.14) whenever this positive finite limit is part of the extraction. 191 4. For a fixed physical affine chart ϕ(z) = z0 +rz, write h◦ϕ+Q log r = g +cv. The conditional law of the physical certificate costs pulled back to this chart and divided by vp is exactly K (v) U (g, e b h; ·). This identity remains valid on conditioning on exterior coarse variables and then choosing a dyadic index measurably from those variables, whenever the conditional interior field marginals are absolutely continuous with respect to the local reference marginals. These are identities at each fixed index, before any limit as v → 0. Changes of density under a fixed reference marginal always use patches whose full dependency region avoids its pinning circle. No uniform absolute-continuity bound for unbounded constant shifts is asserted.

candidates.label: Proposition 16.4
candidates.name: Comparison families
candidates.heading: Proposition 16.4 (Comparison families).
candidates.statement: Consider a limit with the certificate and local-kernel properties of Section 15, obtained with the moment compactness bound of Lemma 14.2. Either of the following assumptions is sufficient for exact-power upper endpoint moment control, compactness of the normalized backward quantum family (v ≤ 1) and each fixed finite forward enlargement, and a finite deterministic upper comparison with D. 1. For some K < ∞, qi ≤ K2−ip for every i ≥ 0. 2. There is an integer i0 ≥ 0 such that 0 < qi < ∞ for every i ≥ i0, and constants 0 < m < M < ∞ such that every own-unit law Gi, i ≥ i0, satisfies T (m, M) with probability at least 1 − ε0. Here ε0 > 0 is chosen sufficiently small, once, for the annulus-coverage threshold with favorable fraction 1/4 and this fixed geometry. The finitely many scales preceding i0 need only have finite endpoint norms and satisfy the given compactness bound. In the second case there is a deterministic T0 < ∞, depending only on m, M and the geometry, such that T−2 0 ≤ bi/bj ≤ T2 0 (i, j ≥ i0). (16.3) In either case, for a finite K′ and every i ≥ 0, ∥X2−i ∥k = qi ≤ K′ 2−ip . (16.4) Each fixed finite forward enlargement has the corresponding bounded-window controls in the retained base units. A change to its own units is allowed once its limiting internal endpoint norm is positive.

candidates.label: Theorem 16.5
candidates.name: Law-level rigidity for the tree model
candidates.heading: Theorem 16.5 (Law-level rigidity for the tree model).
candidates.statement: For every normalized tree law furnished by Proposition 16.4, and every extraction of one of its controlled families after a change of units with positive limiting internal endpoint norm, the optimal constants in (16.8) satisfy c = C > 0. Almost surely, simultaneously on every open set U, FU = CDU . In particular the metric multiplier is deterministic.

candidates.label: Proposition 17.1
candidates.name: Universal comparison of internal norms

manuscripts.title: The canonical massive continuum limit of the two-dimensional O(3) model

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.name: Canonical continuum limit
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1 (Canonical continuum limit).
candidates.statement: For the nearest-neighbor probability (1.1), the periodic thermodynamic limit µβ exists for all sufficiently large β. Both sums in (1.2) are finite, χβ, ξβ > 0, and ξβ → ∞ as β → ∞. The following limits hold through all real values of β tending to infinity. (i) For every finite list of vector tests in C∞ c (R2; R3), the fields (1.3) converge jointly in law and in all joint moments to one common limiting hierarchy. (ii) For every order and every choice of spin components, the associated Schwinger distributions converge in the strong topology of S′((R2)n), that is, uniformly on bounded sets of Schwartz tests. (iii) The limiting hierarchy has susceptibility and second-moment length equal to one. It is the hierarchy constructed in Theorem 1.2, after the unique positive constant length and field rescalings imposing these two normalizations.

candidates.label: Theorem 1.2
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.2.
candidates.statement: There are a dyadic integer L > 1, a constant H > 0, bare couplings βN → ∞, and field normalizations BN > 0, such that aN = L−N , βN = H + log L 2π N + O(log(N + 1)), (1.4) and the following assertions hold for the model (1.1). (i) Every finite list of the variables ϕN (f) = ϕaN ,BN (f), under µβN , converges jointly in law and in all moments. The component Schwinger distributions converge in S′((R2)n) at every order. The same limits are obtained with suitable periodic physical tori tending to the plane as N → ∞. (ii) The limiting Schwinger distributions are Euclidean invariant, internally O(3) invariant, reflec- tion positive, symmetric and clustering. For every component distribution and F ∈ S((R2)n), |Sn(F)| ≤ Cn n! sup x∈(R2)n (1 + |x|2 )2n |F(x)|, with a constant C independent of n. They reconstruct a local, unitary, relativistic theory in 1 + 1 dimensions. (iii) The reconstructed theory has a unique vacuum Ω, a nonzero vacuum complement, and a Hamiltonian Hphys satisfying Hphys Ω⊥ ≥ m1 for some m > 0. 6 (iv) A connected four-point distribution is nonzero on smooth tests with strictly separated time supports. In particular, the limiting field correlations do not satisfy Wick factorization. The trajectory is selected by fixing its terminal kinetic coupling to H at a fixed physical block length.

candidates.label: Corollary 1.3
candidates.heading: Corollary 1.3.
candidates.statement: The canonical limiting hierarchy is Euclidean invariant, internally O(3) invariant, reflection positive, symmetric, and clustering. It satisfies factorial tempered-distribution bounds and reconstructs a local, unitary relativistic theory in 1 + 1 dimensions. The reconstructed Hamiltonian has a unique vacuum, a nonzero vacuum complement, and a strictly positive lower bound on that entire complement. A connected four-point distribution is nonzero on smooth tests with strictly separated time supports.

(2.3)

candidates.label: Theorem 5.1
candidates.name: Exact step and comparison
candidates.heading: Theorem 5.1 (Exact step and comparison).
candidates.statement: Fix υ > 0 sufficiently small. There are choices of L, the canonical caps and comparison weights, P0, and finally H such that integration against one normalized block observation sends every admitted retained density at b ∈ [Hj/2, 2Hj] to an exact representation of the same form in layer j − 1, with all renewed shape caps. The representation may be iterated when its new coupling belongs to [Hj−1/2, 2Hj−1]; that admission is established separately by shooting in Section 6. Its precise coupling is b′ = b + αh(P) + κh(P) b + ∆, |∆| ≤ CLH−1.05 j . (5.1) Here h is the free history, and the bulk scalar, canonical slots, and kicks use the prescriptions of [28, Equation (5.32)] adapted below to S2. All retained norm caps are renewed. For two regular steps with common geometric scales, let λ = b2 − b1, and let u be the fixed weighted shape discrepancy: canonical coefficient differences, regular-error difference divided by its cap, and covering-gas difference divided by its cap. The regular error difference is measured through order k − 1. Then u′ ≤ qu + CL poly(Hj)ϵh + CL(log Hj)C |λ|/Hj, |λ′ − λ| ≤ CLu + CL poly(Hj)ϵh + CL(log Hj)C |λ|/Hj, q < L−2+υ . Signed covering activities are allowed: the logarithm used in constructing the regular exponent is the convergent connected logarithm of the small background factor, based at one. The mandatory-cover factor is retained as a sum, and no logarithm of the full signed density is taken.

candidates.heading: Proposition 10.1 (Moment majorants).
candidates.statement: For every n ≥ 1 and every component array α, the measure Sα n,N is nonnegative. (10.3) for all unit boxes Q1, . . . , Qn. The same bound holds in the periodic infinite-plane state. candidates.label: Proposition 10.2
candidates.name: Continuum limit
candidates.heading: Proposition 10.2 (Continuum limit).
candidates.statement: On every fixed axis or tilted physical torus used in Section 8, all joint moments of the fields ϕN (f) converge for continuous tests. Their finite-dimensional laws converge, and the limiting laws are determined by their moments. The moment measures converge on arbitrary continuous compactly supported tests in the insertion coordinates. In the periodic plane state these assertions hold for compactly supported tests. The same plane limit is obtained by taking the continuum limit on the axis tori and then their exhaustion, or by taking any simultaneous sequence of cutoffs and axis tori for which both the cutoff depth and the doubling index tend to infinity. Finally, let O+ be the rotation with cosine 3/5 and sine 4/5. The Schwinger functions satisfy the Euclidean clustering axiom also for Schwartz tests.

candidates.label: Proposition 11.3
candidates.name: Relativistic reconstruction
candidates.heading: Proposition 11.3 (Relativistic reconstruction).
candidates.statement: The Schwinger functions Sn reconstruct a tempered Wightman theory in 1 + 1 dimensions with a three-component Hermitian scalar field. Its Hilbert space H is positive, its fields are local, and its unitary representation of the Poincaré group satisfies 90 the spectrum condition. The vacuum Ω is unique and normalized. In the positive-time reflection realization of H, Euclidean time translations induce a strongly continuous semigroup e−sHphys , s ≥ 0, with Hphys ≥ 0 and HphysΩ = 0.

candidates.heading: Proposition 11.4 (Gap above the vacuum).
candidates.statement: For the Hamiltonian in Proposition 11.3, the vacuum complement obeys Hphys Ω⊥ ≥ m > 0, (11.5) where m is the common exponent of Proposition 11.2.

candidates.statement: For a sufficiently large fixed terminal coupling H, there exist four smooth compactly supported real tests f1, . . . , f4 with strictly disjoint ordered time ranges for which E 4 Y i=1 ϕ1 (fi) − E[ϕ1 (f1)ϕ1 (f2)]E[ϕ1 (f3)ϕ1 (f4)] − E[ϕ1 (f1)ϕ1 (f3)]E[ϕ1 (f2)ϕ1 (f4)] − E[ϕ1 (f1)ϕ1 (f4)]E[ϕ1 (f2)ϕ1 (f3)] ̸= 0. candidates.label: Proposition 12.1
candidates.name: Canonical increments and comparison estimates

candidates.label: Theorem 2.10
candidates.name: Pure Dobrushin interface
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.10 (Pure Dobrushin interface).

candidates.label: Theorem 9.1

candidates.heading: Theorem 9.1 (Stopping-band transfer).
candidates.statement: Fix an inward or outward band, target, and ambient square chart as in Section 7, with all the stated positive clearances. In the last case the blocker must be the only locally accessible obstruction from that approach, allowing further portions of the same labeled barrier; its ordinary unqueried incidences must be available up to the contacts. candidates.heading: Proposition 4.5 (Joint critical tests with prescribed squares).
candidates.statement: Fix finitely many polygon quads and finitely many closed squares of positive side length, with the squares mutually separated and separated from every quad boundary. For any finite collection of test specifications, the joint law of their exact closed-cell crossing indicators has a common limit along every deterministic good sequence of either model. The limit is continuous in the centers and positive side lengths of the squares throughout the open range where the stated separations hold, and under sufficiently small 38 marked polygonal deformations of the quads. The conclusion remains valid when the centers and side lengths converge to such an admissible fixed configuration as the mesh tends to zero. manuscripts.title: The Gaussian free field limit of integer Lipschitz heights with two-arc boundary data

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: Let D be a bounded smooth simply connected planar domain with two distinct marked boundary points. Let Dδ be simply connected triangular-lattice polygonal approximations with uniformly converging marked boundary parametrizations and edge-midpoint marks, and let hδ have the uniform odd-height law (1.1). There is a constant σ > 0, depending only on the unit triangular-lattice model, such that hδ =⇒ ḡ + σΦD in D′ (D). For every f ∈ C∞ c (D), Ehδ(f) → ∫ D ḡf. Consequently hδ − Ehδ σ =⇒ ΦD in D′ (D). (1.3) All finite vectors of test-function integrals converge jointly to the corresponding Gaussian vectors, and all their mixed moments converge. The constant is specified by the absolutely convergent finite- volume series in Proposition 6.1; in the spectral convention below, σ = 4π √ c∗.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.4
candidates.name: Loop estimates
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.4 (Loop estimates).
candidates.statement: There are constants c0 > 0 and 0 < ρ < 1 such that, for all sufficiently large integer n, the following statements hold. (i) If the interior of a simple contour L contains Λ2n(z), then PL gives probability at least c0 to a loop contained in Λ2n(z) and surrounding Λn(z). (ii) If L has graph inradius n about z, then PL ( at least two loops surround Λρn(z) ) ≤ 1 − c0. (3.3) There is no aspect-ratio or boundary-regularity assumption on L.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.5
candidates.name: Plane law and quantitative local comparison
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.5 (Plane law and quantitative local comparison).
candidates.statement: Free coherent pairs in expanding regular hexagons converge on cylinder events to a law µ∞. This law is invariant under lattice translations, lattice symmetries, global sign changes, and interchange of the colors. If the domain of a finite pair law µE0,η contains a ball of radius L and has no constraints in that ball, then its restriction to a concentric ball of radius r differs from that of µ∞ in total variation by at most C(r/L)α, for L ≫ r ≥ 1. The associated plane height increments exist and have the same spatial symmetries. Every finite feasible prescription of B pins together with W = +1 on finitely many connected paths has positive plane probability.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.7

candidates.heading: Proposition 3.7 (Products of separated pin probabilities).
candidates.statement: For a separated family as above, there are constants 0 < c ≤ C < ∞ such that c ∏ i pi ≤ µ∞ (⋂ i Pi ) ≤ C ∏ i pi. (3.7) The constants depend on the collars, their buffers, the number of obstacles, and ∑ i mi. They do not depend on the mesh, the number or the values of the microscopic B pins, or the probabilities pi. The same estimates hold in all sufficiently large finite free volumes.

candidates.heading: Proposition 4.3 (Interior smearing moments).
candidates.statement: Consider a uniform height problem with boundary values bounded in absolute value by K. Let the center of a radius-a smearing have distance n from the boundary, with 1 ≤ a ≤ c0n for a sufficiently small fixed c0 > 0. Then, for every finite p, ∥ ∑ x wxH(x)∥Lp ≤ Cp ( 1 + √ log(n/a) ) . (4.4) Here Cp depends on p, A, K, but not on boundary regularity. The same statement holds for bounded data on the inner face chain of a dual cut, and in the bounded skeleton faces considered above.

candidates.statement: For every zero-total smearing satisfying (4.1), ∥ ∑ x wxH(x)∥Lp(µ∞) ≤ Cp, p < ∞, (4.8) uniformly in its radius, location, and lattice rotation. The same bound holds in sufficiently larger finite free volumes, for a height anchored outside the construction.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.6
candidates.name: Conditional obstacle moments
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.6 (Conditional obstacle moments).
candidates.statement: Fix finitely many separated interval-compatible obstacles with filled isolating neighborhoods Ui as in Proposition 3.7. Let a test disk lie in a pin-free simply connected neighborhood U0, with room for a surrounding buffered cut whose filled interior lies in U0. Require U0 to be disjoint from every Ui. Let Y be a zero-total smearing in the test disk, satisfying (4.1) at its scale. Conditional on all the pins, ∥Y ∥Lp ≤ Cp (p < ∞). (4.11) The constants depend on the macroscopic arrangement, the weight bound, the number of obstacles, and the bound on W-subpath counts, but not on the mesh or the microscopic pin probabilities. No uniformity as obstacle separations vanish is asserted here.

candidates.label: Corollary 4.7
candidates.name: Equal-offset moments with varying separations
candidates.heading: Corollary 4.7 (Equal-offset moments with varying separations).
candidates.statement: For a nonempty obstacle family in the preceding setup, impose the additional event E = {ti = t1 for every i}. The obstacles may now vary or approach one another, while staying away from a fixed test disk. Fix an annular buffer around that disk, with positive clearance from the disk and with fixed inner and outer radii. Suppose the buffer and its filled interior contain no pins. Suppose that, under conditioning on the pins and E, an exterior search finds a surrounding double-B cut in this buffer, with probability at least c > 0 uniformly in the varying arrangements. Suppose that E can be checked in the exterior of the selected cut, so its strict interior remains free given the trace. Then the zero-total test in that disk has moments bounded uniformly in those arrangements. A sufficient condition is that the cut probability conditional on the pins alone is at least c0 > 0, that P(E | pins) → 1 uniformly along the varying family, and that the same exterior measurability holds.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.1
candidates.name: Reflection positivity with auxiliary phases
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.1 (Reflection positivity with auxiliary phases).
candidates.statement: Let ℓ be a line of lattice sites parallel to a nearest-neighbor direction. The plane law is reflection positive across ℓ. This remains true after adjoining any finite collection of phase fields Zθ(u) = Uθ exp{iθ(H(u) − H(o))}, θ ∈ R, (5.1) where the Uθ’s are independent uniform points of the unit circle, independent of the pair, and o is any anchor. 23 More precisely, let Θℓ denote spatial reflection, and let Aℓ consist of cylinder functions supported in one closed half-plane, with increments evaluated along paths in that half-plane. Then ⟨F, G⟩ℓ = E [ ΘℓF G ] is positive semidefinite. In its quotient completion, normal translation farther into the half-plane by √ 3 is a positive self-adjoint contraction S. Tangential translation by one lattice unit is a commuting unitary operator. On mesh δ, the normal step is √ 3δ.

candidates.statement: The series ∑ j≥0 |Ij| converges. There is a single constant c∗ ≥ 0 such that every limit in Lemma 5.8 has coefficient c∗, and ∑ j≥0 Ij = − π 2 c∗. (5.14) The value is independent of the choice of q satisfying Equation (5.13).

For real f, g ∈ C∞ c (R2) of 30 integral zero, lim δ↓0 E[Hδ(f)Hδ(g)] = c∗ ∫ R2 ̂ f(ζ)̂ g(ζ) |ζ|2 dζ = v 2π ∫∫ R2×R2 f(x) log 1 |x − y| g(y) dx dy. (5.16) The same conclusion holds for tests converging in C∞ c with support in a common compact set.

candidates.label: Corollary 5.11
candidates.name: Reflection null vector
candidates.heading: Corollary 5.11 (Reflection null vector).
candidates.statement: Let ϕ ∈ C∞ c (R2) be supported strictly on one side of a line parallel to a lattice reflection direction. Choose site rows ℓδ converging to that line, still separated from the support by a positive margin. For Xδ = Hδ(∆ϕ), (5.18) its reflection norm at ℓδ tends to zero. This holds in every finite phase augmentation of Proposi- tion 5.1, and also for lattice translations and reflected placements converging to the stated configu- ration.

candidates.label: Proposition 6.1
candidates.name: Finite-volume normalization series
candidates.heading: Proposition 6.1 (Finite-volume normalization series).
candidates.statement: The series of the indicated terms is abso- lutely convergent: ∑ j≥0 |bj0| + ∑ j,s≥0 |bj,s+1 − bjs| < ∞. (6.6) Its value satisfies c∗ = 1 π ∑ j≥0 ⎡ ⎣bj0 + ∑ s≥0 (bj,s+1 − bjs) ⎤ ⎦ > 0, σ = 4π √ c∗. (6.7) Thus the displayed formula specifies a strictly positive universal normalization using only Equa- tions (6.1) to (6.5).

candidates.label: Proposition 7.4
candidates.name: Identity with separated gaps
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.4 (Identity with separated gaps).
candidates.statement: Fix windows, gaps and tests satisfying the preced- ing conditions. Let P = ⋂m i=1 Pi and Jδ = ∏m i=1 P(Pi). For any product Ψδ of unit-modulus phase factors at the representatives vi, E[XδFδΨδ1P ] Jδ −→ 0. (7.13) The phases may have arbitrary fixed real frequencies and the independent Haar lifts of (7.5).
