(7.14)

candidates.label: Proposition 7.6
candidates.name: Bracket identity
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.6 (Bracket identity).
candidates.statement: Fix a window system W for a finite grid L, and either bracket from Lemma 7.1. Let K0, . . . , Kq ⋐ D be disks, with K0 at positive distance from every Kj, j ≥ 1, and let Xδ, Fδ be as in (7.1). Suppose there are two levels ℓ− < ℓ+ in L such that: (i) K0 is strictly between the two levels, and both levels avoid every spectator disk Kj with positive margin; (ii) after opening sufficiently small gaps inside their corresponding windows, every pin arc and spectator disk in the middle band belongs to one of the two strictly separated u-projection families in (7.12). Then lim δ↓0 Eµ±,W δ [Hδ(∆ϕ)Fδ] = 0. (7.19) In particular it applies to products of bounded continuous functions of finitely many smooth zero- total tests in each Kj. There is no disjointness requirement between spectator disks. For this latter class the identity passes to any subsequential distributional limit of the bracket laws. For any fixed bound q on the number of spectator disks these geometric hypotheses can be ar- ranged locally as follows. Fix x ∈ D and ρ > 0 with B(x, ρ) ⊂ D. Take K0 sufficiently small about x, and take at most q spectator disks of sufficiently small radii, all outside B(x, ρ). From a sufficiently dense grid of regular levels one can choose the two levels within a fixed small fraction of ρ above and below x. The choices and smallness bounds depend on q and ρ, not on the number of terms in a later linear combination of such products.

candidates.label: Theorem 8.1
candidates.name: Constant-arc arch estimate
candidates.heading: Theorem 8.1 (Constant-arc arch estimate).
candidates.statement: There are constants M > 1, c, C > 0, and a positive geometric tolerance with the following property. Fix a positive integer N and scales 16r < ℓ1 < · · · < ℓN < R/10, ℓi+1 ≥ Mℓi. (8.2) Suppose that, in QR, the limiting boundary is the single graph y = f(x), with f(0) = f′(0) = 0 and ∥f′∥∞ smaller than the geometric tolerance, and that its inward side is above this graph. The original polygon boundary is a sufficiently fine uniform parametric approximation of this arc and has the same inside and outside away from its shrinking boundary neighborhood. Its approximation error, divided by ℓ1, tends to zero. A smooth boundary has these properties after decreasing the fixed outer scale. Allow, in addition, a fixed finite number of boundary-attached patch replacements as above, whose diameters are sufficiently small relative to the selected scales. Suppose that the actual usable boundary data satisfy η ≥ k − 2 everywhere, η ≥ k on the usable boundary in QR \ Qr, (8.3) where k ∈ Z. For sufficiently small mesh and sufficiently fine boundary and replacement approxi- mations, Pη ( an arch at threshold k surrounds Qr in QR ) ≥ 1 − Ce−cN . (8.4) The constants do not depend on the boundary heights or on the number of vertices in a boundary or separator. They also do not depend on the fixed number of tiny replacements; the required approximation accuracy may do so. There is a reversed statement with η ≤ k + 2, clean data η ≤ k, and a separator at height at most k.

candidates.label: Corollary 8.6
candidates.name: Random traces and tiny boundary replacements
candidates.heading: Corollary 8.6 (Random traces and tiny boundary replacements).
candidates.statement: The arch estimate remains valid conditional on an exterior sigma-field whenever, conditional on that field, the remaining free heights have a uniform Gibbs law and their actual usable boundary data obey (8.3). It also remains valid after a fixed finite number of boundary-attached patches have been removed by exposed simple circuits, provided the same data bounds hold on the new usable boundary. For a prescribed error, first fix a finite collection of arch scales and their boxes. The replacement diameters, boundary approximation errors, and mesh may then be made sufficiently small for all comparisons. The success constants of the resulting blocks have no factor depending on the number of microscopic pins or on the fixed number of replacements.

In that assertion the points and their finite number are fixed before the depths tend to zero.

candidates.statement: For j ≥ 2 and distinct (y, z), L(y, z) = v 2π Tj−2(z). (10.3) The convention is T0 = 1; no centering is made in this identity.

candidates.statement: For distinct points (x, y1, . . . , yj−1), Tj(x, y) = m(x)Tj−1(y) + v j−1 ∑ i=1 GD(x, yi)Tj−2(y \ yi). (10.8) For j = 1 the assertion is T1 = m. candidates.heading: Corollary 3.11 (Sparse contacts with signs).
candidates.statement: Fix a domain, fixed pin values in [−1/2, 1/2], and deterministic sign strings as described above, allowing additional intervals [0, ε]. For every prescribed animal parameter there are a fixed box size and s > 0 such that, except on a bad set with that animal bound, the tested central edges involving nonfixed vertices have |∇h| ≤ 1−s. candidates.heading: Theorem 4.1 (Local reflected comparison).
candidates.statement: Consider the experiments just specified, with |a| + |b| bounded. Assume the conclusions of 3.11, 3.5, and 3.1 for their original marginal laws. Individual reflecting constraints are ordinary one-sided sign walls, not pairs 0 ≤ hx ≤ ε with ε allowed to tend to zero. Fix 0 < r < R < 2, 1 < p < 2, and a desired defect parameter ρ > 0. There are fixed testing parameters, a step length Tρ > 0, good edges Gn and good wall sites Sg n, and positive weights we, wx ≤ 1 with the following properties. For every fixed q < ∞ and A < ∞, the normalized spatial sums of w−q, cluster-size moments, and hole-diameter moments are bounded by deterministic constants outside an event of probability O(n−A). The relevant finite collection of moment orders can be chosen in advance. Let Un be the extension over holes supplied by 3.5, with a fixed choice of the testing parameters. It can be set to zero on the exceptional event. In scaled coordinates, E∥Un∥2 W1,p(n−1Qr) ≤ C, E ∫ n,Qr |Un − u0| −→ 0. (4.4) In a free comparison subtract a local cutoff-weighted average from both Un and z0. Its gradient and dissipation estimates are unchanged. They hold uniformly after replacing z by z/K, K ≥ 1, with bounded rescaled thresholds. Threshold-uniform specialization. With the original marginal moment bounds fixed, EEn (︁ (a − z)+; Qr )︁ + E∥U(a) n ∥2 W1,p(n−1Qr) ≤ C0(1 + a2 ). (4.5) Thus, when a = K ≥ 1 and the observed values satisfy z|P ≥ K, the energy and squared Sobolev norm of (1 − z/K)+ are bounded by 2C0, uniformly in K. For an ordinary simply connected polygon domain with identical fixed boundary data, the exterior- preserving construction in Lemma 4.7 gives a bounded W1,p(R2) extension which is exactly zero outside the lattice polygon. This construction uses connectivity of its zero exterior; it is not asserted for an arbitrary disconnected internal observed set. 18 If QR has no observations or individual walls, and Xn is sampled from normalized ambient volume in Qr, then n∇(Xn,Xn+e)z0 for each fixed lattice step e, n(z0(Xn + i) − z0(Xn)) for each fixed lattice offset i, and n supt≤T0 |zt(Xn) − z0(Xn)| are tight. Sampling is not conditioned on an arbitrarily small random free set. Finally these statements allow a drift difference bounded by cn−2, with bounded support on the macroscopic scale, including a sufficiently small smooth exponential tilt of either marginal. Constants may depend on a fixed bound for c; the smallness needed for the change of marginal law is that in 3.1.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.1
candidates.name: Stationary bulk law
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.1 (Stationary bulk law).
candidates.statement: Under the inputs specified above, the gradient process and its driving Brownian increments, viewed from a uniformly sampled vertex in a compact macroscopic region separated by a fixed positive macroscopic distance from all fixed pins and reflecting sign walls, have a unique local limit. This limit is independent of the bounded boundary data and of the small smooth tilts under consideration. It is stationary in space and time and spatially ergodic. Its local trajectories are continuous and have normal reflection. On a fixed short step, every vertex belongs to a finite transmission cluster; there are almost surely no simultaneous distinct-face contacts. A face visited away from the endpoints of a contact episode has positive reflection impulse in that episode.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.8

candidates.statement: Under the preceding inputs, j(q) is well defined on the vector space of attained slopes and is linear there. If any nonzero slope is attained, every slope in R2 is attained and j(q) = Aq for a finite scalar A. For a stationary comparison with drift difference n−2b(x/n), every subsequential expected macroscopic difference m satisfies ∫ j(∇m) · ∇f = ∫ bf, f ∈ C∞ c (U), (5.6) in each limiting open region U free of observations.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.9
candidates.name: Dirichlet response
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.9 (Dirichlet response).
candidates.statement: Assume the comparison and average estimates hold up to identical fixed boundaries of lattice domains converging to a bounded smooth domain D. Then every slope is attained and the scalar in Proposition 5.8 satisfies 0 < A < ∞. For sufficiently small smooth sources b, the mean response to relative drift n−2b(x/n) converges to A−1 (−∆D)−1 b. For boundary values +λ and −λ on the two marked arcs, the untilted mean converges to their bounded harmonic extension.

candidates.label: Theorem 5.10
candidates.name: Field limit
candidates.heading: Theorem 5.10 (Field limit).
candidates.statement: Under the inputs of this section for the ordinary fixed-boundary domains, the centered affinely interpolated field converges as a random distribution to σ times the Dirichlet Gaussian free field with covariance (−∆D)−1, where σ2 = (vA)−1 . The stiffness is vA, and the limiting mean is the harmonic extension identified in Proposition 5.9.

candidates.label: Proposition 6.6
candidates.name: Varying observed sets and filled values

candidates.statement: The following bounds hold in fixed buffered boxes, uniformly in the mesh and in allowed conditional histories. Its constants depend on b and the fixed box geometry, not on the roughness of the surrounding walls or on the number of chambers in the realization with a common fill. 2. For one chamber, let a lattice-aligned rectangle and its joining buffer lie wholly in the unprescribed accessible interior. Use the relative dual restriction with separate side ports defined in the proof. The number of distinct components of the restricted N graph crossing between two specified opposite sides has a geometric tail. Consequently, if Q0 ⋐ Q1, the number of restricted components in Q1 which meet Q0 and a vertex incident to an edge outside the restriction has a geometric tail, provided the fixed covering rectangles in Q1 \ Q0 and every joining buffer have the same unprescribed interior clearance. Arbitrary admissible (s, W) prescriptions outside a larger buffer are allowed. The same interior assertion holds in the original wired law before removal of its boundary cluster. 3. Counts of distinct free N clusters of the residual kernels enclosing or passing through a fixed aspect-ratio annular shell have moments of every fixed order, uniformly after rescaling the shell down to lattice order. Under a stopping history these are the unsearched clusters. A distinguished wired cluster adds at most one. manuscripts.title: Conditional information under deterministic coordinate sweeps

At time 256d, the images of any k ≤ 7n/8 labels have total-variation distance o(1) from Unif(inj([k], V )). 2. At time 1024d, the images of any k ≤ 15n/16 labels have total-variation distance at most n−3/2, for all sufficiently large d. 3. The full permutation law satisfies ∥q ∗(2048d) d − USn ∥TV → 0.

At time 256d, the images of any at most 7n/8 labels have total-variation distance o(1) from a uniform injective tuple.

Write dim Wi = tiN, t = X i ti, |Si| = 2αiN . If D ⊂ [m] has |D| = xN, x ≤ t, and MK(D) ≤ 2ηN , then xt − x2 2 ≤ X i ti(ti − αi) + ηt + η3 . (8.5)

candidates.label: Proposition 9.1
candidates.name: Certificate pricing
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.1 (Certificate pricing).
candidates.statement: Fix A > 0 and at most two positive constants wi. Typically for nonsingular binary matrices C of size m ∈ IN , the following assertion holds. The typical set is obtained by imposing Proposition 8.1 at a sufficiently large fixed precision depending on A and these constants. Let F denote exposed information which fixes C, a quotient map GC ↠ G, and the data described next. Suppose that, conditionally on F, a tested column v is uniform on {0, 1}m. Partition the layers of G into at most two categories, each a union of whole plateaus. In category i, assume that every height is at least wi; only wi = 1, 2 will be needed. The partition is part of the exposed data. In the quotient of G by the image of v, an outcome may mark some of the retained layers. Require that the marked layers on each plateau form a prefix. The marks may also depend on other random bits in the experiment. Let A be any subevent of this experiment. There is a partition of A into at most 2Nℓ−A classes, constructed before choosing a representative or any target weights, with the following property. Take any nonempty class Aα, any representative outcome in it, and write si and ui for the representative’s sums of the weights νp of the marked and unmarked layers in category i. For any choices 0 ≤ xi ≤ si, Pr(Aα | F) ≤ 2−N(c( P i wixi)− P i E(si,ui,xi)−ℓ−A ). (9.3) Here Aα already includes the restriction to A; the probability is conditioned only on the exposed information. The class count and the estimate are uniform in that information, the quotient, the subevent, and the representative. In particular, the exposed information may include a preceding column that fixes G, provided the tested column remains conditionally uniform.

candidates.heading: Proposition 9.2 (Retained-layer cost).
candidates.statement: Typically for nonsingular binary matrices C of size m ∈ IN , the following estimate holds. Let h ∈ {1, 2} and let v1, . . . , vh be independent uniform columns in {0, 1}m, conditionally on C. Starting with G(0) = GC, let G(j) be the quotient of G(j−1) by the image of vj. For each 1 ≤ j ≤ h, and conditionally on any values of the preceding columns, Pr     X (p,e) retained in G(j−1)↠G(j) νp ≥ σ C, v1, . . . , vj−1     ≤ 2−Nσ/2 . (9.11) The typical set imposes one fixed precision on C, independent of the values of the preceding columns. When these columns occur in a random enlargement of C, no nonsingularity assumption on the destination matrix is required.

manuscripts.title: The sharp singularity rate for biased symmetric sign matrices

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1

candidates.heading: Proposition 2.4 (Column estimate).

manuscripts.title: A CH obstruction to a prescribed categoricity threshold

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.
candidates.statement: Assume the continuum hypothesis. There is an abstract elementary class K in a countable finitary relational language such that (i) LS(K) = ℵ0; (ii) K has at least two nonisomorphic models of cardinality ℶω2 = H(K); (iii) putting Λ = ℶ(2ℵ1 )+ , the class K is categorical in every cardinal µ ≥ Λ. In particular, λ = Λ+ > H(K) is a categoricity cardinal from which downward transfer to H(K) fails.

candidates.label: Theorem 3.13
candidates.heading: Theorem 3.13.
candidates.statement: The pair K = (C, ≤K) of Definition 3.7 is an abstract elementary class in a fixed countable finitary relational language, with LS(K) = ℵ0. It has the union and common-upper-bound properties for every nonempty set-indexed directed family of strong substructures.

candidates.label: Theorem 4.5
candidates.heading: Theorem 4.5.
candidates.statement: The class K has two nonisomorphic models of cardinality ℶη. One has an order sort of cardinality ℵ1, and the other has a countable order sort.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.7

candidates.statement: If M ∈ K and BM is uncountable, then |IM | < Λ.

candidates.label: Theorem 5.10
candidates.heading: Theorem 5.10.
candidates.statement: The class K is categorical in every cardinal µ ≥ Λ.

candidates.label: Corollary 6.1
candidates.heading: Corollary 6.1.
candidates.statement: ZFC proves CH ⇒ Θ. For each fixed Φ as above, it also proves CH ⇒ ¬Φ, and Con(ZFC) =⇒ Con(ZFC + Θ) =⇒ Con(ZFC + ¬Φ). If ZFC is consistent, no such Φ is a theorem of ZFC.

candidates.label: Proposition 6.2
candidates.heading: Proposition 6.2.
candidates.statement: The class K has neither joint embedding nor amalgamation. The failure of amalgamation can be witnessed over a countable model.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.2
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.2.

manuscripts.title: Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes

candidates.label: Theorem 1.2
candidates.name: Uniform eventual categoricity
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.2 (Uniform eventual categoricity).
candidates.statement: For every infinite cardinal λ there is a cardinal µ(λ) ≥ λ such that the following holds for every AEC K with LS(K) ≤ λ: ∃κ ≥ µ(λ) K is categorical in κ  =⇒ ∀κ′ ≥ µ(λ) K is categorical in κ′ . The same threshold is used in the premise and the conclusion.

candidates.label: Theorem 1.3
candidates.name: The qualitative form
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.3 (The qualitative form).
candidates.statement: An AEC categorical in unboundedly many cardinals is categorical on a tail of the cardinals.

candidates.label: Proposition 2.3
candidates.name: The uniform reduction
candidates.heading: Proposition 2.3 (The uniform reduction).
candidates.statement: The uniform assertion in Theorem 1.2 is equivalent to the following qualitative assertion: Every AEC categorical in unboundedly many cardinals is categorical in all cardinals above some bound depending on that AEC.

candidates.label: Theorem 2.6
candidates.name: Order presentation
candidates.heading: Theorem 2.6 (Order presentation).
candidates.statement: Suppose K has arbitrarily large models and LS(K) = ℓ. There are at most ℓ labels, each of positive finite arity, and a functor E from nonempty linear orders and order embeddings to K and strong maps, with the following properties. 1. Every element of E(I) is a label evaluated on an increasing finite list from I. Equality and all structure relations and function values are determined by the labels and the order/equality pattern of the finitely many indices involved. 2. E(I) contains distinct distinguished elements (ai)i∈I. An order embedding f : I −→ J sends ai to af(i), and its action on any labeled element is position substitution. 11 3. For every finite nonempty s ⊆ I, the elements labeled on s form a strong submodel Es(I) of cardinality at most ℓ. For s ⊆ t these submodels are strongly included, and E(I) = S s Es(I). 4. |I| ≤ ∥E(I)∥ ≤ |I| + ℓ. In particular, for every infinite κ ≥ ℓ, K has a model of cardinality exactly κ. Here a subpresentation is identified with its image under the canonical strong map when an inclusion of underlying universes is convenient.

candidates.label: Theorem 3.5
candidates.name: Short-sequence order orbits
candidates.heading: Theorem 3.5 (Short-sequence order orbits).
candidates.statement: Let δ be an infinite limit ordinal and let θ be an infinite cardinal with θ < cf(δ). Two sequences of length at most θ in H(δ) lie in the same Aut(H(δ))-orbit if and only if they have the same order/equality diagram and the same occupancies of all strict slots over their distinct entries.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.9
candidates.name: Alignment of model orbits
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.9 (Alignment of model orbits).
candidates.statement: Fix the record set and orbit naming at an infinite length θ. Let a < µ be categoricity cardinals with a ≥ max(ℓ, θ+). Suppose the following data have one common profile: 1. a presentation E(H(β)) of Cµ, where β is additively indecomposable, |β| = µ, and cf(β) > a; 2. presentations E(H(δ)) of Ca for a cofinal subset of a+ of additively indecomposable ordinals δ of size a and cofinality greater than θ. Then in any copy N of Cµ, every subset of size at most a is contained in A ≤K N of size a such that the orbit name of every θ-tuple in A, computed as a tuple of Ca, is the same as its name computed in N.

candidates.label: Theorem 3.11
candidates.name: Eventual reversal at categoricity cardinals
candidates.heading: Theorem 3.11 (Eventual reversal at categoricity cardinals).
candidates.statement: For each infinite cardinal θ there is a cardinal bK(θ) such that, whenever κ ≥ bK(θ) is a categoricity cardinal, M ∈ K has size κ, f : M −→ M is strong, and ā is a tuple of length at most θ in M, there is a strong g : M −→ M with g(f(ai)) = ai for every coordinate i. The bound concerns all sufficiently large categoricity cardinals, of arbitrary cofinality. No equality of the form κθ = κ is assumed.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.2
candidates.name: Stable diagrams
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.2 (Stable diagrams).
candidates.statement: There is a definable, nondecreasing cardinal function t, with t(σ) > ℓ + σ a categoricity cardinal for every infinite σ, having the following properties. 1. Tuples of length at most σ in models of size at least t(σ) have canonical diagrams. Equality of diagrams is preserved by every strong embedding between such models, and there are at most Bσ diagrams at these lengths. 2. Diagrams include atomic diagrams, respect reindexing and restriction, and are compatible when the bound σ is increased. We denote equality by D(a; M) = D(b; N), suppressing the bound when it is understood. 3. If κ ≥ t(σ) is a categoricity cardinal, equality of diagrams between tuples in κ-models is implemented by a strong map between those models. 4. A possible diagram of a pair of tuples (a, c), of total length at most σ, can be realized over any tuple with the diagram of a in any categoricity model of size at least t(σ). “Possible” means that the diagram occurs in a model in the domain of its definition.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.3
candidates.name: Categoricity at countably cofinal closure points
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.3 (Categoricity at countably cofinal closure points).
candidates.statement: Suppose ζ > ℓ is an infinite cardinal of countable cofinality and t(σ) < ζ for every infinite σ < ζ. Then K is categorical in ζ. Moreover any diagram match between bounded tuples in two ζ-models extends to an isomorphism between those models. Here and throughout the paper, bounded at a level means of cardinality strictly less than that level.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.8
candidates.name: Uniform testing of placed comparisons
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.8 (Uniform testing of placed comparisons).
candidates.statement: There is a definable nondecreasing infinite cardinal function g, depending on K and its fixed presentation, such that the following holds. If I is an infinite well-order, A = E(I), and two placements of a tuple of length at most σ have different placed comparisons over A, then their natural diagrams already differ over a subset of A of size at most g(σ). The bound is independent of |I|.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.9
candidates.name: Compact placement
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.9 (Compact placement).
candidates.statement: Let A = E(I), where I is an infinite well-order, and let χ > ℓ + σ satisfy χσ = χ. Suppose that for every X ⊆ A of size at most χ a possible joint diagram qX(d, X) is prescribed, where d has length at most σ. Assume these prescriptions restrict coherently and that their parameter diagrams are the natural ones of X. Then one placement of d over I realizes all the prescriptions.

candidates.label: Theorem 4.11
candidates.name: Amalgamation at closed levels
candidates.heading: Theorem 4.11 (Amalgamation at closed levels).
candidates.statement: There is an unbounded class of strong-limit cardinals µ of countable cofinality with the following properties. 1. K is categorical in µ, and any two µ-sized strong extensions of a µ-model have a strong amalgam of size µ. 2. If A ≤K B0, B1 all have size µ, and di ∈ Bi are tuples of the same length at most σ < µ, there is such an amalgam identifying d0 with d1 if and only if D(d0, X; B0) = D(d1, X; B1) for every X ⊆ A, |X| ≤ g(σ). 3. There are at most µ singleton types over each µ-model, where type means identification in an amalgam over that model. One may take every sufficiently large strong-limit cardinal of countable cofinality strictly closed under t and g.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.6
candidates.name: The package for single models
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.6 (The package for single models).
candidates.statement: At the sufficiently closed levels supplied by Proposition 4.3, the single K-models, with strong maps as arrows and the original term presentation E, form a working scheme. The levels can be refined to those required in Theorem 4.11 without losing this conclusion.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.7
candidates.name: Naming bounded data
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.7 (Naming bounded data).
candidates.statement: Let C be a working scheme, and fix a bounded list c and its diagram, witnessed at some eligible level. After increasing the fixed lower threshold, the objects with a named realization of this diagram, and arrows preserving the names, form a working scheme. This includes naming enumerations of fixed small strong models in the vertices, with their specified maps. The additional lower bound can be chosen in terms of the original scheme and the cardinality of the named list, independently of the level at which that list was first witnessed.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.8
candidates.name: Obtaining the diagram clause
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.8 (Obtaining the diagram clause).
candidates.statement: Suppose a finite-system scheme has the structural and presentation conditions of Definition 5.2, and is categorical at its eligible levels. For an unbounded supply after refinement, assume the eligible-subclass hypothesis of Convention 5.3. Either of the following inputs supplies the diagram clause, after the indicated closure refinements. 1. For each infinite σ, at all sufficiently large eligible levels, the relation of being sent to another list by an arrow is reversible on lists of cardinality at most σ, and their orbit sets have a bound depending only on σ and the fixed scheme. In this case take stabilization bounds and require enough smaller levels below the receiving level for the bounded arities in use. 2. Same-level arrows preserve isomorphism orbits of bounded lists, and comparisons of such orbits in well-ordered charts are independent of the eligible level. More precisely, for each arity, equivalence of two term patterns by an isomorphism in their respective charts is the same relation on patterns whenever both patterns are bounded at the levels under comparison. The componentwise exhaustion condition follows whenever arrows have only componentwise strong- ness as their additional structural content. For any other arrow condition its exhaustion assertion remains a separate obligation.

candidates.label: Proposition 5.9
candidates.name: Uniform coding of working diagrams
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.9 (Uniform coding of working diagrams).
candidates.statement: There is a fixed first-order set-theoretic definition DF of an equivalence relation on term patterns, uniform in a coherent finite-support template code F. There is a definable cardinal bound bF (σ) such that, on PF (σ), a single back- and-forth test with bound at least bF (σ) computes DF . These definitions do not require the system axioms at the cardinals used for the tests. Suppose, in addition, that F presents a working scheme at unboundedly many eligible strong limit levels of countable cofinality. At every eligible level µ > |F| strictly closed under bF , the working diagram of a bounded term list is exactly its DF -comparison class. The same definition therefore computes the diagrams of every such scheme, including the schemes with fixed named data.

candidates.label: Proposition 6.3
candidates.name: Uniform testing for natural layouts
candidates.heading: Proposition 6.3 (Uniform testing for natural layouts).
candidates.statement: For each fixed natural layout there is a monotone cardinal function g(σ) with the following property. Two placed comparison types of tuples of length at most σ over that layout are equal if and only if they agree on parameter queries of size at most g(σ). The bound is independent of the eligible level. The extra tuple supports may lie in a non-well-ordered extension of the layout. The assertion is uniform when the fixed layout and frozen bounded data range over a fixed set of descriptors of bounded size.

candidates.label: Theorem 6.6
candidates.name: Amalgamation and types for a scheme
candidates.heading: Theorem 6.6 (Amalgamation and types for a scheme).
candidates.statement: At sufficiently closed levels, C has amalgamation. If A → B0, B1 are arrows and vi are equally indexed bounded tuples in Bi, then an amalgam over A identifying v0 and v1 exists if and only if their diagrams agree on all parameter queries in A of size at most g(|vi| + ℵ0). Consequently tp(v/A; B), defined by identification in an amalgam over A, is an equivalence class. It is determined by these bounded diagrams and has an order placement. Restriction of a type means restriction of its actual tuple and parameter diagrams.

candidates.label: Corollary 6.7
candidates.name: Realization into a larger level
candidates.heading: Corollary 6.7 (Realization into a larger level).
candidates.statement: Let ν < µ be sufficiently closed eligible levels. If A → B are ν-objects and A → N is an arrow into a µ-object, then there is an arrow B → N extending the given arrow on A. One may prescribe the image of a tuple of length less than ν whose diagrams over queries in A below ν already match. Types of tuples of length less than ν over A obtained in a larger object are actual ν-types, and the mixed diagram comparisons at those arities agree.

candidates.label: Theorem 6.10
candidates.name: Stationary free extension
candidates.heading: Theorem 6.10 (Stationary free extension).
candidates.statement: Let A → B be an arrow at a sufficiently closed level and let p = tp(v/A), where |v| ≤ σ. There is a specified actual type pB over B, called its free lift, extending p. At every desired query size whose approximation and testing costs are bounded at the originating level, it is computed by transporting sufficiently long approximations in A. At one level this includes every bounded query size; in a mixed-level use the costs must remain below the level of A. It has the following properties. 1. The answer is independent of the approximation sequence, its length, and the auxiliary test size used in its construction. 2. Free lifts commute with restriction of the tuple, are invariant under isomorphisms, and satisfy (pB)C = pC whenever A → B → C. 3. If A has an eligible size ν and B has a larger eligible size, the construction still works for |v| < ν, with its construction thresholds and approximation lists below ν. The restriction to A is the actual ν-type of Corollary 6.7. 4. A sequence from Lemma 6.9 at the fixed threshold c(σ) is bounded code data. If an equally indexed sequence in any sufficiently closed eligible object has the same diagram, it determines a unique corresponding type there by the same majority prescription. Arrows carrying one such sequence to another carry the corresponding type to its free lift. In particular an isomorphism carrying the code sequence transports the type. We say that an actual type over B is free from A when it is the free lift of its restriction to A.

candidates.label: Proposition 6.12
candidates.name: Products of bounded types
candidates.heading: Proposition 6.12 (Products of bounded types).
candidates.statement: For bounded types p(x), q(y) over A, realize p in an extension B ≥ A and then realize qB in a further extension. The joint type of (x, y) over A, denoted p ⊗ q, is independent of all choices. Binary products are symmetric, with the indicated permutation of coordinates. Finite products associate, are permutation invariant, and commute with coordinate projections. Furthermore (p ⊗ q)B = pB ⊗ qB . (4) These assertions hold across eligible levels when all originating arities and uniform testing costs are bounded at the smallest level. If x/B is free from A and x, d have product type over B, then x and (d, e) have product type over A for every bounded tuple e from B.

candidates.label: Proposition 6.13
candidates.name: Local character and continuity
candidates.heading: Proposition 6.13 (Local character and continuity).
candidates.statement: Let (Ai : i < δ) be an increasing chain of objects at one eligible level µ, whose union A has size µ, and let δ be a nonzero limit ordinal. If p = tp(v/A) and either v is finite or |v| < cf(δ), then p is free from some Ai. If, in addition, every restriction tp(v/Ai) is free from a fixed base X ≤ A0, then p is free from X.

candidates.label: Proposition 6.15
candidates.name: Universality of a fresh strip
candidates.heading: Proposition 6.15 (Universality of a fresh strip).
candidates.statement: Let C already satisfy the working package. In addition to its fixed template F, one may use a presentation G with the following properties: it has a fixed set of finite-support labels; every presentation G(J) used below, for an order of size µ, is an object of C at level µ; order embeddings give C-arrows; and the diagrams of its term lists are natural, including in the order enlargements and padded orders used. Assume also that these labels represent every element of G(J). Require µ to exceed the cardinality of the label set of G and to be closed under the bounds below with that cardinal included in their fixed input data. Put A = G(J). Insert into J a fresh convex strip of size µ with countably many disjoint convex substrips, each of size µ, and denote the resulting object by A+. Then every same-level extension of A embeds into A+ over A. In particular this applies to G = F and to well-ordered presentations. No separate union or categoricity assertion for a category of G-presentations is required.

candidates.label: Corollary 6.16
candidates.name: Approximate retractions
candidates.heading: Corollary 6.16 (Approximate retractions).
candidates.statement: For same-level A ≤ B there are arrows (ri : B → A : i < µ) such that, for every a ∈ A, {i < µ : ri(a) ̸= a} < ℵ0. The maps are not asserted to fix all of A at once.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.3
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.3.
candidates.statement: There is a bound function h, depending only on the fixed working scheme, with the following property. Put σ = |u, c| + ℵ0. At sufficiently closed eligible levels, precisely one of the following alternatives holds for q = tp(u, c/A): 1. q is isolated relative to u by a fragment of size at most h(σ); 2. there are an extension A ≤ B at the same level and an extension qB of q such that qB ̸= qfr B, qB ↾ u = tp(u/A)fr B. In particular, every relatively isolated type has an isolating fragment bounded by h(σ), uniformly in the level and in the type.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.5
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.5.
candidates.statement: Let Y be all-dominated over X + b at a sufficiently closed eligible level µ. 1. If an extension N of X contains a tuple b′ of the same type over X, there is an arrow Y −→ N over X sending b to b′. The target may be at a larger eligible level. A prescribed bounded tuple match can be retained whenever its joint type with b over X already agrees. 2. Two all-dominated objects over the same data X + b are isomorphic over those data. The isomorphism may retain a prescribed bounded tuple match of the kind just described. 53 3. In an actual coupling, if a bounded tuple x has product with b over X, then tp(x/Y ) is free from X.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.8
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.8.
candidates.statement: Let λ be a sufficiently closed eligible level, let X be an object there, and let p = tp(b/X) be a finite-tuple type. For every infinite θ < λ there is a same-level extension X ≤ U containing a realization of p such that tp(b, c/X) is isolated relative to b for every c ∈ U with |c| ≤ θ. More generally the assertion holds for a bounded mark b satisfying Definition 7.7, with |b| ≤ θ. The closure requirements at the output level are uniform functions of bounded arities; they do not require θ to have been fixed before the level was chosen.

candidates.label: Theorem 7.9
candidates.heading: Theorem 7.9.
candidates.statement: At sufficiently closed eligible levels, every finite-tuple type p = tp(b/X) has an all-dominated realization: there is Y ≥ X all-dominated over X +b realizing p. More generally this holds for a bounded marginal satisfying Definition 7.7. An all-dominated realization embeds over X, b into any actual ambient containing a realization of that type, with the mixed-level conventions of Proposition 7.5.

candidates.label: Theorem 7.13
candidates.heading: Theorem 7.13.
candidates.statement: Let b = (bi)i<δ be a bounded product-independent list of finite tuples over X at a sufficiently closed eligible level. 1. Its whole type is determined by the product data on finite sublists. Its free lift is product- independent and is the unique whole type with the lifted finite data. 2. The marked marginal tp(b/X) satisfies Definition 7.7. 59 3. There is an all-dominated object over X + b, and it embeds over these data into an actual ambient containing the given list.

candidates.label: Theorem 8.6
candidates.name: The marked-increment working package
candidates.heading: Theorem 8.6 (The marked-increment working package).
candidates.statement: Let C be a working scheme with com- ponentwise arrows and a stationary finite prescription as in Definition 8.1. Assume the eligible- subclass hypothesis of Convention 5.3. On an unbounded further class of sufficiently closed eligible levels, Cb is again a working scheme, with componentwise arrows, fixed template Fb, and mixed arrows between these levels. The output class retains the eligible-subclass hypothesis. The added language and bound recipes at this step have set-sized bounds in the input template and prescription. Thus the construction can be performed at each fixed finite depth without class-sized parameters or a language size depending on the level.

candidates.label: Proposition 9.1
candidates.name: Type correspondence under projection
candidates.heading: Proposition 9.1 (Type correspondence under projection).
candidates.statement: Let P : C −→ D forget some compo- nents of systems. Suppose that both schemes satisfy the working package, that P takes objects and arrows to objects and arrows, including mixed arrows, and that the following diagram comparison holds: for bounded tuples in the retained sorts, equality of their C-diagrams is equivalent to equality of their D-diagrams after projection. The comparisons are made at arities bounded at both levels when levels differ. 69 At sufficiently closed levels, restriction induces a bijection on types of bounded tuples in any fixed list of retained sorts, given by tpC(v/X) 7−→ tpD(v/PX). The parameters on the left are all of X, including its forgotten components. The bijection commutes with restriction and isomorphisms, and with free lifting along arrows, including mixed arrows when the tuple arities and the required testing bounds lie below the smaller level. It also takes witnessed free products to their projected witnessed free products.

candidates.label: Corollary 9.2
candidates.name: Lifting an extension of a projection
candidates.heading: Corollary 9.2 (Lifting an extension of a projection).
candidates.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 9.1, let X and Z be at the same eligible level, and let PX −→ Z be an arrow. There are a C-extension X −→ X∗ and a D-arrow Z −→ PX∗ whose composite on PX is the projection of X −→ X∗.

candidates.label: Theorem 9.3
candidates.name: Finite marked systems
candidates.heading: Theorem 9.3 (Finite marked systems).
candidates.statement: Start with the single-model scheme, allowing fixed bounded named data of a fixed diagram. Let r be a prescribed, definable, isomorphism-invariant stationary type of a finite tuple in its root sort. Stationarity here includes free lifting under mixed arrows at eligible levels. For each finite n, the n-fold marked increment construction gives a working scheme Cn at sufficiently closed levels. Its objects are systems indexed by the subsets of {1, . . . , n}, with the prescribed marks and componentwise strong arrows. 71 For s ⊆ {1, . . . , n}, retaining the axes in s in their induced order gives a projection Ps : Cn −→ C|s|. Every such projection takes objects and arrows to objects and arrows, including mixed arrows, and preserves and reflects diagram equality on bounded tuples in its retained sorts. It consequently has the exact type correspondence of Proposition 9.1. The type in the root sort lying over r exists uniquely over every whole system and lifts freely. These conclusions include the projection to the base root and each single-axis projection. In a single-axis projection the upper object is all-dominated over its lower object together with the prescribed mark; forgetting other axes does not remove that assertion.

candidates.label: Theorem 9.6
candidates.name: Amalgamated boundary completion
candidates.heading: Theorem 9.6 (Amalgamated boundary completion).
candidates.statement: For each finite n, at sufficiently closed levels the following holds. If J and K are Cn-objects at the same level and h : ∂J → ∂K is a boundary map, there are arrows K −→ K∗ , J −→ K∗ in Cn such that the second restricts to the composite of h with the first on every proper projection. The extension is in the same scheme and at the same level. No assertion about completion between distinct levels is needed here.

candidates.label: Theorem 9.8
candidates.name: Exact boundary lifting
candidates.heading: Theorem 9.8 (Exact boundary lifting).
candidates.statement: For each finite n, at further sufficiently closed levels every boundary isomorphism h : ∂J ∼ = −→ ∂K between Cn-objects at the same level extends to an isomorphism J ∼ = K onto the given target. All the prescribed marks and bounded named data are preserved.

candidates.label: Proposition 10.2
candidates.name: A minimal type
candidates.heading: Proposition 10.2 (A minimal type).
candidates.statement: There is a sufficiently closed single-model level λ0, a model M0 ∈ K of size λ0, and a nonalgebraic singleton type p0 over M0 such that, over every M0 ≤K A ∈ K of size λ0, there is exactly one nonalgebraic extension of p0. This extension is its free lift.

candidates.label: Theorem 10.5
candidates.name: The geometry of the minimal type
candidates.heading: Theorem 10.5 (The geometry of the minimal type).
candidates.statement: On P(M), for every M0 ≤K M of size at least λ0, the preceding finite independence is the independence relation of a finitary pregeometry. Its closure, denoted by clM , has the following properties. 1. For finite F ⊆ P(M) and any maximal independent S ⊆ F, the set clM (F) consists exactly of those points that do not independently extend S. Equivalently, clM (F) is the set of points forced by F. 2. Strong embeddings over M0 preserve and reflect finite closure. If M0 ≤K A ≤K M, then P(A) is relatively closed in P(M). 3. For finite F, | clM (F)| ≤ λ0. For every infinite F ⊆ P(M), | clM (F)| ≤ |F| + λ0. 80 In particular bases exist, all bases have the same cardinality, and each point of the span of a basis has finite basis support.

candidates.label: Proposition 10.6
candidates.name: Pointed working levels
candidates.heading: Proposition 10.6 (Pointed working levels).
candidates.statement: At all sufficiently closed levels µ above the bounds for |m̄0| = λ0, models with a distinguished strong copy of M0 whose enumeration has diagram ∆ form a categorical working scheme. Arrows preserve the indicated copy pointwise. For a pointed model B at such a level, p0 has a unique nonalgebraic extension pB over B; it is its free lift. This family lifts freely along pointed arrows, including the permitted mixed arrows. Naming further bounded data of a fixed diagram within the base does not change type computation over the whole base.

candidates.label: Proposition 10.7
candidates.name: Change of base for the geometry
candidates.heading: Proposition 10.7 (Change of base for the geometry).
candidates.statement: Let B be a pointed model at a sufficiently closed level much larger than λ0. A finite list of points in an extension of B is independent over the closed set P(B) in the geometry of Theorem 10.5 if and only if its type over B is the product of the corresponding copies of pB.

candidates.label: Theorem 10.9
candidates.name: No proper pair with unchanged points at one level
candidates.heading: Theorem 10.9 (No proper pair with unchanged points at one level).
candidates.statement: There is a sufficiently large cardinal λ > λ0 such that there is no proper strong inclusion A <K B of pointed models of size λ with P(A) = P(B).

candidates.label: Corollary 10.10
candidates.name: No-growth and rank on the entire tail
candidates.heading: Corollary 10.10 (No-growth and rank on the entire tail).
candidates.statement: Increase the threshold λ if necessary to include the bounds for the fixed point diagram. In arbitrary cardinalities, if A ≤K B are pointed models with ∥A∥ ≥ λ and P(A) = P(B), then A = B. Moreover, for every pointed model M with ∥M∥ > λ, |P(M)| = rk(P(M)) = ∥M∥. The point sets of strong submodels are relatively closed, and relative bases and finite basis supports are available as in Theorem 10.5; no eligibility condition is imposed on these arbitrary cardinalities.

candidates.label: Proposition 11.6
candidates.name: Tiled presentations
candidates.heading: Proposition 11.6 (Tiled presentations).
candidates.statement: Let L be admissible and let µ be sufficiently large for the pointed pregeometry and the no-proper-pair conclusion. The order template E gives a presentation in GL as follows. Choose a fixed initial order carrying the whole enumeration of M0. For each active label t, choose a tile Tt, preceded by a buffer Bt, and concatenate these finitely many pairs after the initial order, in any fixed order. Every tile and buffer is a dense linear order without endpoints of size µ. In vertex s retain the initial order, all buffers, and just the tiles with labels t ⊆ s. These presentations have the following properties. 1. Each active relative piece has rank µ. 2. Order embeddings of the corresponding tiles and buffers, fixing the initial pointed data, induce arrows, including between different eligible levels. 3. A presentation has an extension by an arrow gaining µ independent complementary coordi- nates at every active label simultaneously. 4. Tiles may be chosen with µ pairwise disjoint convex substrips, each of size µ. Further insertions of such substrips preserve the preceding assertions and the naturalness of the underlying K-diagrams. No categoricity assumption about GL is used here.

candidates.label: Proposition 11.7
candidates.name: Conditional working package
candidates.heading: Proposition 11.7 (Conditional working package).
candidates.statement: Fix an admissible shape L. Suppose that GL is categorical at every level in an unbounded class of eligible levels closed sufficiently for the preceding constructions. Assume also the eligible-subclass hypothesis of Convention 5.3. On an unbounded further class of sufficiently closed levels, it satisfies the full working package of Definition 5.2, with its actual system isomorphisms and its arrows from Definition 11.1. The resulting diagrams, saturation, and calculus include mixed arrows between eligible levels, and the output class retains the eligible-subclass hypothesis. The closure requirements are uniform in the finite shape and the fixed pointed template. They use only the smaller and larger input levels specified by the general working-package construction.

candidates.label: Theorem 11.9
candidates.name: Classification with prescribed basis maps
candidates.heading: Theorem 11.9 (Classification with prescribed basis maps).
candidates.statement: For each finite admissible shape L, at all sufficiently closed uniform levels µ, the following assertions hold. 1. If X, Y ∈ GL, an isomorphism e∅ : X∅ ≃ Y∅ and arbitrary bijections between the chosen nonroot pieces of X and Y extend to a system isomorphism X ≃ Y . In particular GL is categorical at these levels. 2. Suppose X → Y and X → Z are arrows in GL. Choose pieces of X, extend them to pieces of Y and Z, and prescribe a bijection CY s ≃ CZ s for every active label s. Then there is a system isomorphism Y ≃X Z realizing every prescribed bijection. The complementary cardinalities may be less than µ, and zero is allowed. The level requirements are uniform over the finitely many shapes at any fixed number of axes.

candidates.label: Theorem 12.2
candidates.name: Exact geometric boundary lifting
candidates.heading: Theorem 12.2 (Exact geometric boundary lifting).
candidates.statement: For every finite allowed shape, at all sufficiently closed uniform levels, every prescribed boundary isomorphism between two systems of that shape extends to a pointed isomorphism of their tops. The top isomorphism, together with its prescribed restrictions, is an isomorphism of the systems. The refinements of the eligible levels needed for a fixed shape use only the one-dimensional bounds for its working scheme, the bounds for its tiling layouts, and the corresponding assertions for shapes on fewer axes. In particular these refinements have the uniformity specified in Section 13.

candidates.label: Proposition 13.1
candidates.name: Uniform finite-depth definitions
candidates.heading: Proposition 13.1 (Uniform finite-depth definitions).
candidates.statement: Fix the set code for K from Proposition 2.3, its order template, and the fixed data used in either of the two applications. There are a set D of normalized finite descriptors and fixed first-order formulas of set theory with the following properties. 1. Given d ∈ D and an infinite cardinal µ, the formulas define sets of standardized objects and arrows. For marked descriptors these sets are obtained by a finite recursion whose length is an input; at eligible levels they give precisely the categories Cn. For a geometric descriptor they give the systems GL and their arrows. 2. The formulas define orbit comparison, comparison of realized types over a base, relative isolation, the prescribed root marginal, and the finite projection and boundary conditions. On levels with the requisite working package these definitions agree with their mathematical meanings in the preceding sections. 3. There is one unary adequacy formula, with a descriptor as parameter, which can assert any of the packages needed during the finite inductions: the individual working conditions, the chart clause using DF , the projection and type conditions, amalgamated completion, exact boundary lifting, or the geometric categoricity and basis conditions. Its use does not require a formula for a previously chosen closure function. 4. All candidate term templates, named patterns, and finite descriptors needed in the two inductions can be chosen from D. In particular, their codes have one set-sized bound independent of the finite depth and of the level cardinal. These are definitions at every cardinal; a definition by itself makes no claim that the cardinal is eligible.

candidates.label: Theorem 13.5
candidates.name: Common levels for all finite depths
candidates.heading: Theorem 13.5 (Common levels for all finite depths).
candidates.statement: With the fixed data of either application and the constructions proved in the preceding sections, there is an unbounded class of countable-cofinality strong limit cardinals at which all its finite-depth conclusions hold simultaneously. In the marked application this includes the working packages, projection and type correspondences, amalgamated completion, and exact boundary lifting for every Cn, uniformly over the root prescription codes realized at arbitrarily large eligible single-model levels. In the geometric application it includes categoricity, the working packages, basis lifting, and exact boundary lifting for every finite shape. One such common level may be chosen above any specified set of fixed cardinal thresholds.

candidates.label: Theorem 14.3
candidates.name: Exact lifting at every larger cardinal
candidates.heading: Theorem 14.3 (Exact lifting at every larger cardinal).
candidates.statement: For every finite allowed shape and every monotone assignment (κs : s ∈ L) of cardinals at least γ, any prescribed boundary isomorphism between two systems with that assignment extends to an isomorphism of their tops.

candidates.label: Corollary 14.4
candidates.name: Pointed categoricity on a tail
candidates.heading: Corollary 14.4 (Pointed categoricity on a tail).
candidates.statement: For every cardinal κ ≥ γ, any two models of cardinality κ carrying the fixed point pattern are pointedly isomorphic.

candidates.label: Theorem 14.5
candidates.name: Categoricity on a tail
candidates.heading: Theorem 14.5 (Categoricity on a tail).
candidates.statement: If an AEC K is categorical in unboundedly many cardinals, then there is a cardinal θ such that K is categorical in every cardinal κ ≥ θ. Here categoricity includes the existence of a model at each such cardinal.

manuscripts.title: Rigidity of the Turing degrees

candidates.heading: Theorem 3.1 (Slaman–Woodin).
candidates.statement: For every π ∈ Aut(DT , ≤T ) there is an arithmetic function ̂ F : 2N → 2N such that [ ̂ F(A)]T = π([A]T ) for every A ⊆ N.

candidates.label: Proposition 4.1
candidates.name: Recovery from four values
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.1 (Recovery from four values).
candidates.statement: Let F : R → 2N be Borel with countable fibers, and suppose F(x + y) ≤T F(x) ⊕ F(y) (x, y ∈ R). For every irrational t ∈ (0, 1) there is a comeager set Gt ⊆ R2 such that for each (u, v) ∈ Gt there is a rational δ ∈ (0, 1) for which C(t) ≤T F(u) ⊕ F(u − v) ⊕ F(v − u + δt) ⊕ F(v − u + δ(t − 1)). (4.1)

candidates.heading: Corollary 5.1.
candidates.statement: The Turing-degree ordering is biinterpretable without parameters with full second- order arithmetic, in the sense of [11, Definition 7.5.1].

manuscripts.title: Single-fold Diophantine representations

candidates.label: Theorem 1.1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.

candidates.label: Corollary 1.2
candidates.name: Undecidability with an at-most-one-solution promise
candidates.heading: Corollary 1.2 (Undecidability with an at-most-one-solution promise).
candidates.statement: There exist integers m, D ≥ 1 for which no algorithm has the following property: on every input polynomial F ∈ Z[W1, . . . , Wm] of total degree at most D satisfying the promise #{w ∈ Nm : F(w) = 0} ≤ 1, the algorithm halts and correctly decides whether this set is nonempty.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.1
candidates.heading: Proposition 3.1.
candidates.statement: The group E(Q) has rank one and torsion subgroup T = {O, (0, 0), (5, 0), (−5, 0)}. Consequently there exists P ∈ E(Q) such that every rational point has a unique expression nP + t, with n ∈ Z and t ∈ T .

candidates.label: Proposition 4.2
candidates.heading: Proposition 4.2.
candidates.statement: There are a total function g : N → N, a real constant δ > 0, and an integer u0 ≥ 4 such that the graph of g has a single-fold Diophantine representation, including uniqueness of its output and every auxiliary coordinate for each input, and δ(log u)2 < log g(u) < u log u (u ≥ u0). (7)

candidates.label: Proposition 5.2
candidates.heading: Proposition 5.2.
candidates.statement: Suppose that g : N → N has a complete single-fold graph and that there are fixed constants δ > 0 and u0 ∈ N, with u0 ≥ 4, such that δ(log u)2 < log g(u) < u log u (u ≥ u0). (14) Then the relation Pow(b, n, c) ⇐⇒ b ≥ 2 and c = bn (b, n, c ∈ N) has a complete single-fold representation. In particular, for each b ≥ 2 and n ∈ N, the output c and all auxiliary variables are jointly unique.

candidates.label: Proposition 6.1
candidates.heading: Proposition 6.1.
candidates.statement: The relation x ≼ y on N2 has a complete single-fold Diophantine representation.

candidates.label: Proposition 7.2
candidates.heading: Proposition 7.2.
candidates.statement: Fix n ≥ 1 and a deterministic counter machine with finitely many states and counters, instructions INC and TESTDEC, and one halt state. Initialize each counter by a fixed choice of an input coordinate ai or zero. There is a finite system of integer polynomial equations in a ∈ Nn and natural auxiliary variables such that, for every input a, the complete auxiliary tuple has exactly one solution when the initialized machine halts, and no solution when it does not halt.

manuscripts.title: Choiceless polynomial time with counting does not capture polynomial time

candidates.label: Theorem 1
candidates.heading: Theorem 1.
candidates.statement: The query Q on all finite structures in the fixed vocabulary τ of eight binary relations is isomorphism-invariant and decidable in deterministic polynomial time, but is not definable in full choiceless polynomial time with counting.

candidates.statement: The query Q is isomorphism-invariant and decidable in deterministic polynomial time from an ordered encoding of its input structure.

candidates.heading: Corollary 9.

Every object in X, including every recursive constituent of each of its members, has a K-support of length at most 2L(q log3 N)2. All these supports can be padded to the common positive length s = l 2L(q log3 N + 1)2 m + 1 = Oq L(1 + log L)2 . (14)

candidates.label: Proposition 13

candidates.statement: Let r ≥ 1, and suppose 7r + 7(6r/c)3/2 + 1 ≤ M. (18) If two r-tuples in the same Āb have equal CM -types, then some k ∈ K maps the first tuple to the second. The corresponding statement for empty tuples holds without any width hypothesis.

candidates.label: Theorem 14

candidates.heading: Theorem 14 (Transfer through small supports).
candidates.statement: Let A0, A1 be nonempty finite structures in the same binary relational vocabulary, and let Ki ≤ Aut(Ai) for i ∈ {0, 1}. Let s, m, M be positive integers satisfying max{4, m + 1}s ≤ M. Assume the following two properties. 1. A0 and A1 satisfy the same CM sentences. 2. In each Ai, any two tuples of length at most max{2, m}s with the same CM type lie in the same Ki orbit. manuscripts.title: Witnessed symmetric choice is strictly stronger than choiceless polynomial time with counting

The CPT sentences in (ii) may use counting and hereditarily finite sets of unrestricted finite rank.

candidates.label: Proposition 3.3

candidates.statement: For every L ≥ 2 and b ∈ FVL 3 , the maps ha,k define a faithful action of H by automorphisms of the entire τ-structure Ab. candidates.heading: Proposition 4.4 (A total all-input definition).

candidates.heading: Theorem 1.1.

T is left cancellative and conical, has conditional joins, and has heights and costs satisfying Equation (2.1). 6 2. Every valid finite overlap prescription on copies of T is realized by left translations x 7→ lix in T, with exactly the prescribed identifications. 3. For a, b ∈ T with b ̸= 1, and every ideal U ⊆↓ a, there are µ distinct elements m with mb = ae, m ̸⊑ a, ↓ m∩ ↓ a = U, n ∨ m = ae (n ⊑ a, n / ∈ U). (2.2) The cones of distinct elements in this family intersect exactly in aeT. Moreover |T \eT| = µ. 4.
